政策法规国土安全部 (DHS)重要#留学生与 OPT#入境与签证签发

美国国土安全部发布最终规则，取消F、J、I类非移民的“身份持续期”制度

发布日期 2026年7月17日生效日期 2026年9月15日

美国国土安全部(DHS)发布最终规则，将F类学生、J类交流访问者和I类外国媒体代表原有的不设固定期限的“身份持续期”(duration of status)入境许可改为固定期限入境，并新增延期停留申请程序。该规则是对2025年8月公布的拟议规则的最终修订，原定于2026年9月15日生效，但因被列为须经国会审查的重大规则，生效日期仍可能发生变化。

要点

  • DHS将F、J、I类非移民的入境许可由身份持续期改为固定期限。
  • 针对这些类别新增了延期停留申请程序。
  • 该规则修订8 CFR第214、248和274a部分内容，是对2025年8月28日公布拟议规则的最终定稿。
  • DHS表示此举将使移民官员有更多机会核实相关人员是否遵守规定，以应对非法滞留和欺诈问题。
  • 生效日期为2026年9月15日，但由于该规则被列为须经国会审查的重大规则,生效日期甚至规则本身仍可能被更改。

影响对象

受影响人群包括F-1学生、J-1交流访问者、I类外国媒体代表及其随行家属，以及接收他们的学校和项目主办方。

建议行动

受影响人员应与所在学校的指定负责官员(DSO)、项目负责人或移民律师确认新的固定入境期限和延期要求，并在2026年9月15日生效前留意国会审查可能带来的变化。

全文翻译

摘要:
SUMMARY:
美国国土安全部(DHS)正在修订其法规,将F、J和I类别的准许停留期限由“身份有效期”改为固定期限的准许停留,并对准许入境和延期要求作出其他修改。本最终规则将为这些非移民类别提供额外的保护和监督,并使国土安全部能够更好地评估这些非移民在美国临时停留期间是否维持身份。本最终规则是对2025年8月28日在《联邦公报》上发布的涉及该主题的拟议规则的修订。
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is amending its regulations to change the admission period in the F, J, and I classifications from duration of status to an admission for a fixed time period, and additional changes to admission and extension requirements. This final rule will provide additional protections and oversight of these nonimmigrant categories and will allow DHS to better evaluate whether these nonimmigrants are maintaining status while temporarily in the United States. This final rule provides amendments to the proposed rule covering this topic that was published in the Federal Register on August 28, 2025.
日期:
DATES:
本规则已被归类为须接受国会审查的重大规则。生效日期为2026年9月15日。但是,如果在国会审查结束时生效日期发生变更,国土安全部将在《联邦公报》上发布文件,以确定实际生效日期或终止本规则。
This rule has been classified as a major rule subject to congressional review. The effective date is September 15, 2026. However, at the conclusion of the congressional review, if the effective date has been changed, DHS will publish a document in the Federal Register to establish the actual effective date or to terminate the rule.

二、执行摘要
II. Executive Summary
A. 监管行动的目的
A. Purpose of the Regulatory Action
在美国学习并参加交流访问学者项目和学术项目，使外国人能够接触到世界知名的个性化教学和教育项目。同样，美国也允许外国新闻和媒体从业人员作为其境外雇佣工作的一部分进入美国。数百万外国人以F类（学术学生）、[1] J类（交流访问者）、[2]和I类（外国信息媒体代表）[3]非移民身份暂时来到美国。[4]
Studying and participating in exchange visitor and academic programs in the United States offers aliens access to world-renowned, individualized instructional and educational programs. Similarly, the United States allows foreign news and media members access to the United States as part of their foreign employment. Millions of aliens have come to the United States on a temporary basis in the F (academic student),[1] J (exchange visitor),[2] and I (representatives of foreign information media) [3] nonimmigrant classifications.[4]
与大多数被准予入境至特定离境日期为止的非移民类别不同，F类、J类和I类（来自中华人民共和国（PRC）的部分I类非移民除外）非移民被准许在美国停留的时间不特定，以便从事其各自非移民类别所授权的活动。这段不特定的时间被称为“身份有效期”（D/S）。对于F类学术学生而言，D/S通常是指学生在经国土安全部（DHS）批准的教育机构攻读全日制课程期间，或在完成学业后从事经授权的实习培训期间，再加上经授权的离境时间。[5] 对于J类交流访问者而言，D/S是指交流访问者参加经授权项目的期间，再加上经授权的离境时间。[6] 对于I类外国信息媒体代表而言，D/S是指其在美国履行境外雇佣职责的期间。[7] 对于F类、J类或I类主申请人的随行家属而言，只要该家属也遵守其各自类别的相关要求，其D/S通常与主申请人的准许入境期限相对应。[8]
Unlike aliens in most nonimmigrant classifications who are admitted until a specific departure date, F, J, and I (except for some I nonimmigrants from the People's Republic of China (PRC)) nonimmigrants are admitted into the United States for an unspecified period of time to engage in activities authorized under their respective nonimmigrant classifications. This unspecified period of time is referred to as “duration of status” (D/S). D/S for F academic students is generally the time during which a student is pursuing a full course of study at an educational institution approved by DHS, or engaging in authorized practical training following completion of studies, plus authorized time to depart the country.[5] D/S for J exchange visitors is the time during which an exchange visitor is participating in an authorized program, plus authorized time to depart the country.[6] D/S for I representatives of foreign information media is the duration of their foreign employment duties in the United States.[7] For dependents of principal F, J, or I nonimmigrants, D/S generally corresponds with the principal's period of admission so long as the dependents are also complying with the requirements of their particular classifications.[8]
自1978年首次为F类非移民、1985年首次为J类和I类非移民引入D/S制度以来，[9] 每年获准入境美国的F类、J类和I类非移民人数已显著增加。[10] 仅在2024财政年度，F类身份的入境人数就超过180万人（原文第44977页），较美国移民归化局（INS，现已并入国土安全部）1979年首次采用D/S入境制度时有大幅上升，且较2023财政年度增长超过11%。[11] 例如，在1980至1981学年，F类身份的入境人数约为26万人。[12] 过去数十年间，J类非移民人数也出现了类似的增长。在2024财政年度，J类身份的入境人数超过50万人，较1985年入境美国的141,213人次增长超过300%，且较2023财政年度增长超过7%。[13] 最后，在2024财政年度，美国I类外国媒体代表非移民的入境人数为37,330人次，是1985年16,753人次入境人数的两倍多，较上一财政年度增长近15%。[14]
Since D/S was first introduced in 1978 for F nonimmigrants and in 1985 for J and I nonimmigrants,[9] the number of F, J, and I nonimmigrants admitted each year into the United States has significantly increased.[10] In fiscal year (FY)2024 alone, there were over 1.8 ( printed page 44977) million admissions in F status, a dramatic rise from when the legacy U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service (INS) first shifted to D/S admission in 1979 and more than an 11 percent increase since FY 2023.[11] For example, in the 1980-81 school year, there were approximately 260,000 admissions in F status.[12] Similar growth in the J nonimmigrant population has also occurred over the past decades. In FY 2024, there were over 500,000 admissions in J status, up over 300 percent from the 141,213 J admissions into the United States in 1985 and up over 7 percent since FY 2023.[13] Finally, there were 37,330 admissions for I nonimmigrant foreign media representatives in the United States in FY 2024, over double the 16,753 admissions into the U.S. in 1985 and a nearly 15 percent increase from the prior fiscal year.[14]
在D/S制度下，F类学术学生、J类交流访问者和I类信息媒体代表的数量大幅增加，这对国土安全部在这些非移民人员在美国期间进行监测和监督的能力构成了挑战。在其D/S期间，即一段没有特定结束日期的准许入境期间，这些非移民人员除少数有限情形外，无需与国土安全部直接互动，例如在申请选择性实习培训（OPT）的工作许可时，或在未能维持身份后申请恢复身份时。总体而言，D/S入境制度未能为移民官员提供足够的预先确定的机会，以直接核实获准此类非移民身份的外国人在美国期间仅从事其各自类别所授权的活动。这反过来削弱了国土安全部有效执行与非法滞留相关的法定不可准入事由的能力，并为欺诈和滥用行为创造了可乘之机。
The significant increase in the volume of F academic students, J exchange visitors, and I representatives of information media under D/S poses a challenge to DHS's ability to monitor and oversee these nonimmigrants while they are in the United States. During the length of their stay for D/S, a period of admission without a specified end date, these nonimmigrants are not required to have direct interaction with DHS, except for a few limited instances, such as when applying for employment authorization for optional practical training (OPT), or for reinstatement if they have failed to maintain status. Admission for D/S, in general, does not afford immigration officers enough predetermined opportunities to directly verify that aliens granted such nonimmigrant statuses are engaging only in those activities their respective classifications authorize while they are in the United States. In turn, this has undermined DHS's ability to effectively enforce compliance with the statutory inadmissibility grounds related to unlawful presence and has created incentives for fraud and abuse.
对于F和J签证持有者，《移民与国籍法》（INA）明确规定，外国人必须在外国拥有住所且无放弃该住所的意图，并寻求临时进入美国，[15] 然而，国土安全部（DHS）发现许多学生和交流访问者以学生或交流访问者身份滞留数十年的事例。[16]
For F and J visa holders, the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) specifically states that aliens must have a residence in a foreign country which they have no intention of abandoning and seek to enter the United States temporarily,[15] yet, DHS has many examples of students and exchange visitors staying for decades in their student or exchange visitor status.[16]
“9·11”事件凸显了学生签证可能被滥用的风险。“9·11”事件发生后，一项题为《通过移民政策打击恐怖主义》的国土安全总统令指示，除其他事项外，应制定一项计划以追踪外国学生的身份状态。该指令还要求政府制定指导方针，其中可能包括诸如限制学生身份期限等控制机制。[17] “9·11”委员会重申了追踪外国学生并对学生签证实施更严格管控的必要性。[18] 基于这些指令和下文所述的法定授权，学生与交流访问者项目（SEVP）由此设立，电子化的学生与交流访问者信息系统（SEVIS）也得以实施。SEVIS是国土安全部用于存储和处理在美外国学生及交流访问者信息的计算机系统。
The events of 9/11 highlighted the potential for abuse of the student visa. In the wake of 9/11, a Homeland Security Presidential Directive titled, Combating Terrorism Through Immigration Policies directed, among other things, that a program be developed to track the status of foreign students. It also mandated that the government develop guidelines that may include control mechanisms such as limited duration of student status.[17] The 9/11 Commission reiterated the need to track foreign students and place tighter controls on student visas.[18] From these mandates and the statutory authorities described below, the Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP) was created, and the electronic Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS) was implemented. SEVIS is a DHS computer system that stores and processes information about foreign students and exchange visitors in the U.S.
SEVIS确保各政府机构掌握与非移民学生和交流访问者相关的关键数据，以维护国家安全。SEVIS同时落实了1996年《非法移民改革和移民责任法》（IIRIRA，公法104-208，编入《美国法典》第8编第1372节）第641条的规定，该条要求国土安全部在非移民学生和交流访问者在美停留期间持续收集其最新信息。此外，2001年《通过提供拦截和阻止恐怖主义所需的适当工具来团结和加强美国法》（美国爱国者法案，公法107-56，修订IIRIRA第641条）第416条，要求全面实施并扩展SEVIS系统。
SEVIS ensures government agencies have essential data related to nonimmigrant students and exchange visitors to preserve national security. SEVIS also implements Section 641 of the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996 (IIRIRA), Public Law 104-208 (codified at 8 U.S.C. 1372), which requires DHS to collect current information from nonimmigrant students and exchange visitors continually during their stay in the United States. In addition, section 416 of the Uniting and Strengthening America by Providing Appropriate Tools Required to Intercept and Obstruct Terrorism Act of 2001 (USA PATRIOT Act), Public Law 107-56 (amending IIRIRA sec. 641), mandated full implementation and expansion of SEVIS.
鉴于上述法律要求和相关关切，国土安全部认为，允许F、J和I类非移民以“在美停留期限”（D/S）方式入境已不再适当。本最终规则以恢复规定具体终止日期的入境停留期限，取代适用于F、J和I类非移民的D/S框架。希望在固定入境期限届满后继续留在美国的非移民，须直接向国土安全部申请延长停留期限（EOS）[19]，或通过出境后再入境的方式重新获准入境。国土安全部预计，许多F、J和I类非移民将能够在其入境期限内完成各自的相关活动。然而，对于无法在该期限内完成活动者，一般可向移民官员申请延长其入境期限。国土安全部认为，这一流程将有助于减轻那些意图利用这些项目、以非临时方式在美国生活（这与适用于其非移民身份的基础法律条文相悖）的外国人所带来的风险。
Given these mandates and concerns, DHS believes that the admission of F, J, and I nonimmigrants for D/S is not appropriate. The final rule replaces the D/S framework for F, J, and I nonimmigrants with a return to an admission period with a specific date upon which an authorized stay ends. Nonimmigrants who would like to stay in the United States beyond their fixed period of admission will need to apply directly to DHS for an extension of stay (EOS) [19] or gain readmission by traveling abroad and re-entering the United States. DHS anticipates that many F, J, and I nonimmigrants will be able to complete their respective activities within their period of admission. However, those who are unable will generally be able to request an extension of their period of admission from an immigration officer. DHS believes that this process will help to mitigate risks posed by aliens who seek to exploit these programs and live in the United States on a non-temporary basis in contradiction with the underlying statutory language that applies to their nonimmigrant status.
以固定期限的授权停留期限取代以“在美停留期限”（D/S）方式的入境许可，这与大多数其他非移民类别的做法相一致。[20] （印刷页第44978页）此举将为这些非移民类别提供额外的保护和监管，并使国土安全部能够更好地评估这些非移民在美临时停留期间是否维持其身份。国土安全部认为，此项要求不会对F、J和I类非移民造成不当负担。相反，为F、J和I类非移民设定一个固定的授权停留期限，要求其在该specific入境期限届满前申请延长停留、变更非移民身份，或以其他方式获得继续留在美国的授权（例如调整身份），这与适用于大多数其他非移民类别的要求相一致，也与1979年之前适用于F-1学生的做法相一致。[21]
Replacing admissions for D/S with admissions for a fixed time period of authorized stay is consistent with most other nonimmigrant categories.[20] It will ( printed page 44978) provide additional protections and oversight of these nonimmigrant categories and will allow DHS to better evaluate whether these nonimmigrants are maintaining status while temporarily in the United States. DHS does not believe such a requirement will place an undue burden on F, J, and I nonimmigrants. Rather, providing F, J, and I nonimmigrants a fixed time period of authorized stay that will require them to apply to extend their stay, change their nonimmigrant status, or otherwise obtain authorization to remain in the United States ( e.g., adjustment of status) by the end of this specific admission period is consistent with requirements applicable to most other nonimmigrant classifications and consistent with the practices for F-1 students prior to 1979.[21]
这些变化将确保国土安全部（DHS）拥有一个有效机制，定期直接评估这些非移民是否遵守其身份分类条件及美国移民法律，并及时获取关于这些外国人在美国临时逗留期间已从事及计划从事活动的准确信息。如果移民官员发现属于上述分类之一的非移民已逾期停留或以其他方式违反其身份，该外国人将就《移民与国籍法》（INA）项下与非法居留相关的不可准入法定事由而累积非法居留时间。外国人在美国的非法居留可能导致其在离开美国后变得不可准入。[22]由于这种不可准入性，该外国人可能丧失获得非移民签证或移民签证、准入美国或须以可准入性为条件的其他福利（例如调整身份为合法永久居民）的资格。[23]这将鼓励外国人维持合法身份，并减少F、J和I类非移民在其项目、实践培训或与I类身份相符的活动或任务结束后非法滞留美国的情形。国土安全部认为，加强监督将遏制F、J或I类非移民从事欺诈和滥用行为，并在加强国家安全的同时，增强这些非移民分类的完整性。
These changes will ensure that DHS has an effective mechanism to periodically and directly assess whether these nonimmigrants are complying with the conditions of their classifications and U.S. immigration laws, and to obtain timely and accurate information about the activities these aliens have engaged in and plan to engage in during their temporary stay in the United States. If immigration officers discover a nonimmigrant in one of these classifications has overstayed or otherwise violated his or her status, the alien will accrue unlawful presence for purposes of unlawful presence-related statutory grounds of inadmissibility under the INA. Unlawful presence in the United States may result in an alien becoming inadmissible upon departing the United States.[22] As a result of this inadmissibility, the alien may become ineligible for a nonimmigrant or immigrant visa, admission to the United States, or benefits for which admissibility is required, such as adjustment of status to that of a lawful permanent resident.[23] This will encourage aliens to maintain lawful status and reduce instances in which F, J, and I nonimmigrants unlawfully remain in the United States after their program, practical training, or activities or assignments consistent with the I classification end. DHS believes this greater oversight will deter F, J, or I nonimmigrants from engaging in fraud and abuse and will strengthen the integrity of these nonimmigrant classifications while enhancing national security.
国土安全部认为，本规则各项新规定的条款各自独立运作。然而，为维护国土安全部制定本规则的目标，国土安全部在法规文本中增加了关于条款可分割性的规定，以便在必要时，即使某一条款无法执行，该法规仍可继续运作。
DHS believes that the provisions of each new regulatory amendment function independently of other provisions. However, to protect DHS's goals for this rule, DHS added regulatory text stating that the provisions are severable so that, if necessary, the regulations may continue to function even if a provision is rendered inoperable.
B. 公众参与，意见概述
B. Public Participation—Overview of Comments
2025年8月28日，国土安全部发布了题为《为非移民学术学生、交流访问者及外国新闻媒体代表设立固定准入期限及延长停留期限（EOS）程序》的拟议规则制定通知（NPRM）（联邦公报第90卷第42070页）。公众被给予32天时间就该拟议规则提出意见，并被给予60天时间就该拟议规则制定通知中“文书削减法案”部分所述的信息收集提出意见。国土安全部共收到近22,000条公众意见。如需查看相关意见，请访问 https://www.regulations.gov ，并在“搜索”框中输入本规则制定的电子案卷编号：DHS Docket No. ICEB-2025-0001。
On August 28, 2025, DHS published a notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM), Establishing a Fixed Time Period of Admission and an Extension of Stay (EOS) Procedure for Nonimmigrant Academic Students, Exchange Visitors, and Representatives of Foreign Information Media (90 FR 42070). The public was given 32 days to comment on the proposed rule and 60 days to comment on the information collections described in the Paperwork Reduction Act section of the NPRM. DHS received close to 22,000 public comments. To see comments go to https://www.regulations.gov and enter this rulemaking's eDocket number: DHS Docket No. ICEB-2025-0001 in the “Search” box.
C. 变更摘要
C. Summary of Changes
经过对所收到公众意见的审慎考虑，国土安全部对该拟议规则制定通知中提出的法规文本作出了若干修改。[24]然而，该通知中提出的大部分变更均已被采纳。与该拟议规则制定通知相比的变更摘要见下文第V.A节。如本序言其他部分详细讨论，本最终规则对《联邦法规汇编》（CFR）所作的变更包括以下内容：
Following careful consideration of public comments received, DHS has made several changes to the regulatory text proposed in the NPRM.[24] However, most of the changes proposed in the NPRM have been adopted. A summary of the changes as compared to the NPRM is outlined in section V.A. below. As discussed in detail elsewhere in this preamble, the changes this final rule makes to the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) include the following:
修订8 CFR第214.1条《准入、延期及身份维持要求》，具体内容如下：
Amend8 CFR 214.1, Requirements for admission, extension, and maintenance of status, by:
删除所有关于F、J和I类非移民“在身份有效期内”（D/S）的提法；
Striking all references to D/S for F, J, and I nonimmigrants;
阐明F和J类非移民寻求准入的要求，包括境外旅行后重新准入的情形，以及获批OPT（实习培训）和学术培训者的要求；
Describing requirements for F and J nonimmigrants seeking admission, including after travel abroad and those approved for OPT and academic training;
更新交叉引用，并澄清适用于在口岸（POE）申请准入的F和J类非移民的自动签证有效期延长条款的准入标准，该条款适用于仅在毗邻领土或邻近岛屿逗留且缺席不超过30天的情形；

Outlining the process for EOS applications for F, J, and I nonimmigrants;
对于在本规则生效后的头6个月内，如正在申请完成后实习培训（OPT）或STEM OPT的就业授权，提供暂缓提交延长停留期限（EOS）申请的短期宽限；

以通用语言取代对具体表格名称及编号的提及，以适应未来表格名称及编号的变更；并且
Replacing references to specific form names and numbers with general language, to account for future changes to form names and numbers; and
明确规定已及时提交延长居留期限(EOS)申请的F-1学生,在入境许可期限届满后,直至美国公民及移民服务局(USCIS)审理完该延长居留期限申请之前,将获准继续完成全日制学业。

赋予美国国土安全部(DHS)在必要时推迟实施关于禁止变更学校、教育目标及教育阶段规定的权力;
Providing DHS the ability to delay implementation of the prohibition on changing schools, educational objectives, and levels if needed;
明确在读F-1学生可获准延长居留期限(EOS)的情形;
Clarifying the circumstances under which a continuing F-1 student may be granted an EOS;
将F-1非移民在完成学业课程或经授权的完成学业后实习培训期限届满后,为离开美国做准备所允许的期限从60天缩短为30天;

为那些D/S身份在本规则生效后不久即将到期的J-1非移民提供临时宽限,允许其申请延长身份期限(EOS),并在新Form DS-2019所列期限内继续工作,无论EOS申请审理需要多长时间;
Providing a temporary reprieve for those J-1s whose D/S status expires shortly after the rule takes effect by allowing them to apply for EOS and continue to work for the duration of the time on their new Form DS-2019 regardless of how long the EOS application takes to adjudicate;
规定如果项目结束日期被缩短,J-1交流访问者及其任何随行的J-2家属必须在新的项目结束日期起30天内离开美国,或在该30天期限内寻求维持合法身份;
Requiring that if the program end date is shortened, the J-1 exchange visitor and any J-2 accompanying dependents must leave the United States within 30 days from the new program end date or otherwise seek to maintain lawful status in that 30-day period;
规定负责官员(RO)在为交流访问者提交延长现行项目结束日期的逾期申请时所应承担的职责;
Providing the responsibilities of the responsible officer (RO) when submitting late requests for extension of current program end date for exchange visitors;
明确I类非移民根据8 CFR 274a.12(b)(20)的规定,在其及时提交的延长身份期限(EOS)申请待决期间,可继续为其外国雇主工作长达240天(但来自中华人民共和国的I类非移民可继续工作的期限为90天);
Clarifying that I nonimmigrants are authorized to continue working in the United States for their foreign employer, under8 CFR 274a.12(b)(20), for up to 240 days (with the exception of I nonimmigrants from the PRC who may continue working for up to 90 days) while their timely filed EOS application is pending;
删除F、J和I非移民类别中所有关于“身份期限”和/或“雇佣期限”的表述;以及
Striking all references to “duration of status” and/or “duration of employment” for the F, J, and I nonimmigrant classifications; and
增加一项可分割性条款。如因任何原因本规则的任何条款未能实施,其余条款仍可依照本规则所述目的继续实施。
Including a severability clause. In the event that any provision of this rule is not implemented for whatever reason, the remaining provisions can be implemented in accordance with the stated purposes of this rule.
修订8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(ii)(E),将延迟或暂停实施8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(ii)(A)至(C)的权限限制为自本规则生效之日起两年的期限,因为该条款并非需要无限期适用。
Amending8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(ii)(E) to limit the ability to delay or suspend the implementation of 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(ii)(A) through (C) for a period of two years from the effective date of the rule since this provision is not needed indefinitely.
通过以下方式修订8 CFR 248.1“资格”条款:
Amend8 CFR 248.1, Eligibility, by:
确立规则,用以确定在本最终规则生效日期之前已获批准更改身份申请、随后离开美国、并在本最终规则生效日期之后寻求入境的F类或J类非移民的停留期限;以及
Establishing requirements to determine the period of stay for F or J nonimmigrants whose change of status application was approved before the final rule's effective date and who depart the United States, then seek admission after the final rule's effective date; and
将国土安全部(DHS)长期以来的政策法典化,即如果及时提交更改为其他非移民身份(包括F或J身份)申请的外国人在申请待决期间离开美国,国土安全部将视该申请为自动放弃。
Codifying the long-standing policy under which DHS deems abandoned an application to change to another nonimmigrant status, including F or J status, if the alien who timely filed the application departs the United States while the application is pending.

D. 成本与收益概述
D. Summary of the Costs and Benefits
目前,F类(学术学生)、J类(交流访问者)以及大多数I类(外国新闻媒体代表)非移民均依据“身份期限”(D/S)框架获准入境美国。然而,该框架对国土安全部有效监测和监督这些非移民,以评估其是否遵守其身份条款和条件以及是否存在国家安全隐患的能力构成了挑战。为解决这些薄弱环节,国土安全部正以固定期限的入境许可取代F、J和I非移民的身份期限(D/S)安排。以固定期限许可F、J和I类别外国人入境,将要求所有希望在其特定获准入境期限之后继续停留在美国的F、J和I类非移民,如身在美国境内,须向美国公民及移民服务局(USCIS)申请延长停留授权,从而要求国土安全部对该外国人是否可延长在美停留期限进行定期评估。这一变化将给F、J和I类非移民以及学校和交流访问者项目发起人带来一定的增量成本,但同时也将通过由移民官员评估和确定这些非移民的适当停留期限,维护F、J和I项目的完整性。
Currently, aliens in the F (academic student), J (exchange visitor), and most I (representatives of foreign information media) nonimmigrant classifications are admitted to the United States under the D/S framework. However, this framework poses a challenge to DHS's ability to efficiently monitor and oversee these nonimmigrants to assess whether these nonimmigrants are complying with the terms and conditions of their status and whether they present national security concerns. To address these vulnerabilities, DHS is replacing D/S with an admission for a fixed time period for F, J, and I nonimmigrants. Admitting aliens in the F, J, and I classifications for a fixed period of time will require all F, J, and I nonimmigrants who wish to remain in the United States beyond their specific authorized admission period to apply for authorization to extend their stay with USCIS if in the United States, thus requiring periodic assessments by DHS in order for the alien to remain in the United States for a longer period. This change will impose incremental costs on F, J, and I nonimmigrants as well as schools and exchange visitor program sponsors but will in turn protect the integrity of the F, J, and I programs by having immigration officers evaluate and assess the appropriate length of stay for these nonimmigrants.
该规则的分析期涵盖10年,并假定该规则将于2026年生效。因此,分析期为2027年至2036年。本分析使用两种贴现率估算未来成本的年化价值:3%和7%。行政管理和预算局(OMB)在A-4号通告中建议,当法规影响私人消费时使用3%的贴现率(printed page 44980),而在评估主要影响或改变私营部门资本使用的法规时使用7%的贴现率。贴现率反映了较早发生的收益或成本具有更高价值这一事实。该规则的年化成本将在4.431亿美元至4.486亿美元之间(分别采用3%和7%的贴现率)。若仅考虑美国相关方,年成本在1.199亿美元至1.251亿美元之间(分别采用3%和7%的贴现率)。
The period of analysis for the rule covered 10 years and assumed the rule would go into effect in 2026. Therefore, the analysis period goes from 2027 through 2036. This analysis estimates the annualized value of future costs using two discount rates: 3 percent and 7 percent. In Circular A-4, OMB recommends that a three percent ( printed page 44980) discount rate be used when a regulation affects private consumption, and a seven percent discount rate be used in evaluating a regulation that will mainly displace or alter the use of capital in the private sector. The discount rate accounts for how benefits or costs that occur sooner are more valuable. The rule will have an annualized cost ranging from $443.1 million to $448.6 million (with 3 and 7 percent discount rates, respectively). When considering U.S. parties only, annual costs range from $119.9 million to $125.1 million (with 3- and 7-percent discount rates, respectively).
三、背景与目的
III. Background and Purpose
A. 法律授权
A. Legal Authority
国土安全部部长(以下简称“部长”)实施本规则中监管修正案的授权见于移民法的多项条款。2002年《国土安全法》(HSA)(公法第107-296号,116 Stat. 2135)第102条,即6 U.S.C. 112,以及《移民与国籍法》(INA)第103(a)(1)和(3)条,即8 U.S.C. 1103(a)(1)、(3),赋予部长负责管理和执行美国移民与归化法律的职责。INA第214(a)条,即8 U.S.C. 1184(a),赋予部长通过法规规定任何外国人以非移民身份入境的时间和条件的权力,包括F、J和I类非移民外国人。另见6 U.S.C. 271(a)(3)、(b)(描述美国公民及移民服务局(USCIS)的某些职能和权限,包括USCIS制定全国移民服务政策与优先事项以及裁决福利申请的权力),以及6 U.S.C. 252(a)(4)(描述美国移民及海关执法局(ICE)收集有关外国学生和交流项目参与者信息,并利用该信息执行其执法职能的权力)。
The authority of the Secretary of Homeland Security (the Secretary) to implement the regulatory amendments in this rule can be found in various provisions of the immigration laws. Section 102 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (HSA) (Pub. L. 107-296, 116 Stat. 2135), 6 U.S.C. 112, and section 103(a)(1) and (3) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1103 (a)(1), (3), charge the Secretary with the administration and enforcement of the immigration and naturalization laws of the United States. Section 214(a) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1184(a), gives the Secretary the authority to prescribe, by regulation, the time and conditions of admission of any alien as a nonimmigrant, including F, J, and I nonimmigrant aliens. See also6 U.S.C. 271(a)(3), (b) (describing certain USCIS functions and authorities, including USCIS's authority to establish national immigration services policies and priorities and adjudicate benefits applications) and 6 U.S.C. 252(a)(4) (describing the authority of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to collect information relating to foreign students and exchange program participants and to use such information to carry out its enforcement functions).
INA第248条,即8 U.S.C. 1258,允许国土安全部(DHS)准许某些非移民将其身份从一种非移民身份转换为另一种非移民身份,但有某些例外情形,只要其持续保持现有非移民身份,且未根据INA第212(a)(9)(B)(i)条,即8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(9)(B)(i),被认定为不可入境。与延长停留期限类似,身份转换的裁决属于自由裁量决定。[25] 此外,INA第274A条,即8 U.S.C. 1324a,规范了依法律规定或经部长自由裁量授权在美国获准就业的外国人的雇佣事宜。
Section 248 of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1258, permits DHS to allow certain nonimmigrants to change their status from one nonimmigrant status to another nonimmigrant status, with certain exceptions, as long as they continue to maintain their current nonimmigrant status and are not inadmissible under section 212(a)(9)(B)(i) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(9)(B)(i). Similar to extensions of stay, change of status adjudications are discretionary determinations.[25] Also, section 274A of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1324a, governs the employment of aliens who are authorized to be employed in the United States by statute or in the discretion of the Secretary.
最后,INA规定了谁可以F、J或I类非移民身份获准入境。具体而言,INA第101(a)(15)(F)(i)条,即8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(15)(F)(i),为符合条件可修读全日制课程、希望临时且仅为在经学生及交流访问者项目(SEVP)认证的学术或语言培训学校修读全日制课程的目的入境美国的真实学生等人员设立了F类非移民身份,同时也适用于该等外国人的配偶及21岁以下未婚子女。另见INA第214(m)条,即8 U.S.C. 1184(m)(对某些意图在公立中小学就读的外国人的非移民入境予以限制)。
Finally, the INA establishes who may be admitted as F, J, or I nonimmigrants. Specifically, section 101(a)(15)(F)(i) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(15)(F)(i), established the F nonimmigrant classification for, among others, bona fide students qualified to pursue a full course of study who wish to enter the United States temporarily and solely for the purpose of pursuing a full course of study at an academic or language training school certified by the SEVP, as well as for the spouse and unmarried children under the age of 21 of such aliens. See also INA 214(m), 8 U.S.C. 1184(m) (limiting the admission of nonimmigrants for certain aliens who intend to study at public elementary and secondary schools).
INA第101(a)(15)(J)条,即8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(15)(J),为希望临时来美国且无意放弃其在外国的居所、参加由美国国务院(DoS)指定的交流访问者项目的外国人设立了J类非移民身份,同时也适用于某些J-1类别中该等外国人的配偶及21岁以下未婚子女。
Section 101(a)(15)(J) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(15)(J), established the J nonimmigrant classification for aliens who wish to come to the United States temporarily and have no intention of abandoning their residence in a foreign country, to participate in exchange visitor programs designated by the DoS, as well as for the spouses and unmarried children under the age of 21 of such aliens in certain J-1 categories.
INA第101(a)(15)(I)条,即8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(15)(I),基于对等原则,为寻求入境美国从事该职业的外国新闻媒体(如新闻、广播、电影、印刷媒体)真实代表设立了I类非移民身份,同时也适用于该等外国人的配偶及子女。
Section 101(a)(15)(I) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(15)(I), established, upon a basis of reciprocity, the I nonimmigrant classification for bona fide representatives of foreign information media (such as press, radio, film, print) seeking to enter the United States to engage in such vocation, as well as for the spouses and children of such aliens.
在国土安全部(DHS)内部,学生和交流访问者项目(SEVP)由美国移民及海关执法局(ICE)负责管理。SEVP依据多项法定授权获得授权,管理有关非移民学生和交流访问者信息的收集项目。《1996年非法移民改革和移民责任法》(IIRIRA)第641条授权建立一个项目,利用电子报告技术(在可行的情况下),收集学校和交流访问者项目就F类和J类非移民在美停留期间所提供的当前及持续性信息。根据这一法定授权,DHS依照《国土安全总统令第2号》(HSPD-2)《通过移民政策打击恐怖主义》(2001年10月29日,经修订)(https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CPRT-110HPRT39618/pdf/CPRT-110HPRT39618.pdf)以及《2002年加强边境安全和签证入境改革法》(EBSVERA)第502条(公法107-173号,《美国法规大全》第116卷第543页,第563页(2002年5月14日))管理这些项目。HSPD-2要求国土安全部部长对获准接收F类非移民的院校进行定期、持续的审查,并将合规检查纳入其中,审查内容包括记录保存和报告要求的遵守情况。EBSVERA第502条指示部长在该法颁布后2年内,对所有获准接受F类学生就读的学校进行关于遵守《美国法典》第8编第1101(a)(15)(F)条和第1372条所规定的记录保存和报告要求的审查,此后每2年审查一次。
Within DHS, SEVP is administered by ICE. SEVP is authorized to administer the program to collect information related to nonimmigrant students and exchange visitors under various statutory authorities. Section 641 of IIRIRA authorizes the creation of a program to collect current and ongoing information provided by schools and exchange visitor programs regarding F and J nonimmigrants during the course of their stays in the United States, using electronic reporting technology where practicable. Consistent with this statutory authority, DHS manages these programs pursuant to Homeland Security Presidential Directive-2 (HSPD-2), Combating Terrorism Through Immigration Policies (Oct. 29, 2001), as amended, ( https://www.gpo.gov/​fdsys/​pkg/​CPRT-110HPRT39618/​pdf/​CPRT-110HPRT39618.pdf), and section 502 of the Enhanced Border Security and Visa Entry Reform Act of 2002, Public Law 107-173, 116 Stat. 543, 563 (May 14, 2002) (EBSVERA). HSPD-2 requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to conduct periodic, ongoing reviews of institutions certified to accept F nonimmigrants, and to include checks for compliance with recordkeeping and reporting requirements. Section 502 of EBSVERA directs the Secretary to review the compliance with recordkeeping and reporting requirements under 8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(15)(F) and 1372 of all schools approved for attendance by F students within 2 years of enactment, and every 2 years thereafter.
B. 背景
B. Background
1. F类身份
1. F Classification
《移民与国籍法》(INA)第101(a)(15)(F)(i)条,即《美国法典》第8编第1101(a)(15)(F)(i)条,允许真正的学生身份外国人暂时入境美国,其唯一目的是在经认可的学院、大学、神学院、音乐学院、学术性高中、小学或其他学术性语言培训项目中修读全日制课程。主申请人被归类为F-1非移民,其可随行或随后前来团聚的配偶及子女则被归类为F-2受抚养人。[26]
Section 101(a)(15)(F)(i) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(15)(F)(i), permits aliens who are bona fide students to temporarily be admitted to the United States solely for the purpose for pursuing a full course of study at an established college, university, seminary, conservatory, academic high school, elementary school, or other academic language training program. Principal applicants are categorized as F-1 nonimmigrants and their spouses and children who may accompany or follow to join as F-2 dependents.[26]
从1973年到1979年,F类学生获准入境为期一年,如证明其维持合法身份,可获准延长停留期限(EOS),每次最长延长12个月。[27]然而,鉴于当时在美非移民学生数量庞大,以及持续处理其EOS申请的必要性,原移民归化局(legacy INS)于1978年7月26日提议修订相关法规,允许F-1学生获准以其学生身份持续期间(D/S)入境。[28]原移民归化局解释称,这一变更将有利于非移民学生的入境便利,为政府节省资金和人力,并使资源利用更为高效。[29]1978年11月22日,一项最终规则公布,修订《联邦法规汇编》(CFR)第8编第214部分的相关规定,允许原移民归化局准许F-1学生以D/S方式入境。[30]该规则于1979年1月1日生效。
From 1973 to 1979, F students were admitted for one year and could be granted an EOS in increments of up to 12 months if they established that they were maintaining status.[27] However, on July 26, 1978, given the large number of nonimmigrant students in the United States at the time and the need to continually process their EOS applications, legacy INS proposed amending the regulations to permit F-1 students to be admitted for the duration of their status as students.[28] Legacy INS explained the changes would facilitate the admission of nonimmigrant students, provide dollar and manpower savings to the Government, and permit more efficient use of resources.[29] On November 22, 1978, a final rule was published to amend the regulations at 8 CFR 214 to allow the legacy INS to admit F-1 students for a D/S period.[30] That rule became effective on January 1, 1979.
(印刷页第44981页)
( printed page 44981)
此后,在1981年1月23日至1991年10月29日期间,移民归化局又四次修订了涉及F-1学生入境期限的法规。[31]1981年1月23日,一项规则将F-1非移民的入境期限改为固定期限,即完成课程所需的时间,并可根据具体情况逐案申请延长停留期限(EOS)。[32]原移民归化局解释称,这一变更是必要的,因为以D/S方式准许非移民学生入境,导致对外国学生的管控存疑,并造成记录保存方面的问题。[33]
Subsequently, between January 23, 1981, and October 29, 1991, the INS amended the regulations addressing admission periods for F-1 students four more times.[31] On January 23, 1981, a rule changed admission for F-1 nonimmigrants to a fixed period of admission, i.e., the time necessary to complete the course of study, with the opportunity for an EOS on a case-by-case basis.[32] Legacy INS explained this was necessary because admitting nonimmigrants students for D/S resulted in questionable control over foreign students and contributed to problems in record keeping.[33]
1983年4月5日,D/S制度得以恢复,同时还实施了其他一些变更,包括为学校间转学制定新的通知程序、改进指定学校官员(DSO)[34]的报告要求、限制在同一教育层级内的就读次数,以及要求F-1学生在申请延长停留期限(EOS)时(如适用)同时申请转学,以在相同教育程度层级修读另一教育课程。[35]
On April 5, 1983, D/S was reinstituted with, among other changes, the implementation of new notification procedures for transfers between schools, improved reporting requirements for Designated School Officials (DSOs),[34] a limit for enrollment in one educational level, and a requirement for F-1 students to apply for an EOS and, if applicable, a school transfer to pursue another educational program at the same level of educational attainment.[35]
1987年4月22日,一项最终规则列明了允许F-1学生在保持D/S身份的同时将课程负荷降至全日制以下的医疗和学业原因,并明确了何时必须申请延长停留期限(EOS)或恢复身份。[36]
On April 22, 1987, a final rule outlined medical and academic reasons that would allow F-1 students to drop below a full-time course of study while remaining in D/S status and clarified when an EOS or reinstatement must be requested.[36]
最后，1991年,相关法规被修订以实施1990年《移民法》(IMMACT 90)第221(a)条,公法101-649号,104 Stat. 4978,该法为F-1学生设立了为期三年的校外项目,[37]并明确了F-1学生利用I-20表格申请在学延期(EOS)和工作许可的程序。[38]该规则还授权指定校方负责人(DSO)在F-1学生因有力的学术或医疗原因无法在项目结束日期前完成其教育项目时,给予项目延期(实质上是一种在学延期),并随后通知移民归化局(INS)该项延期情况。[39]此后,根据1991年最终规则,国土安全部(DHS)一直依赖指定校方负责人报告学生身份、发放项目延期并在项目及学校之间转移学生。这些非移民学生的信息现已被纳入学生与交流访问者信息系统(SEVIS)进行追踪,以确保政府机构掌握与非移民学生相关的必要数据,从而维护国家安全。这与《非法移民改革和移民责任法》(IIRIRA)、《美国爱国者法案》(公法107-56号)的要求以及“9·11委员会报告”的建议相一致。2020年曾提出对F类学生的在校期限（D/S）作出修改，但该提案已于2021年撤回。[40]
Finally, in 1991, the regulations were revised to implement Section 221(a) of the Immigration Act of 1990 (IMMACT 90), Public Law 101-649, 104 Stat. 4978, which established a three-year off-campus program for F-1 students,[37] and clarified the procedures for F-1 students seeking EOS and employment authorization utilizing the Form I-20.[38] The rule also gave DSOs the authority to grant program extensions (essentially an EOS) for F-1 students with a compelling academic or medical reason that prevented them from completing their educational program by a program end date and then to notify INS of the extension.[39] Since then, and pursuant to the 1991 final rule, the DHS has relied on DSOs to report on student status, issue program extensions, and transfer students between programs and schools. Information from these nonimmigrant students is now tracked in SEVIS to ensure government agencies have essential data related to nonimmigrant students to preserve national security. This is consistent with the requirements in IIRIRA, the USA PATRIOT Act, Public Law 107-56, and the recommendations of the 9/11 Commission Report. Changes to D/S were proposed for F students in 2020, but the proposal was withdrawn in 2021.[40]
2. J类签证分类
2. J Classification
J类非移民签证分类由1961年《相互教育与文化交流法》创设,该法又称1961年《富布赖特－海斯法案》,公法87-256号,75 Stat. 527（22 U.S.C. 2451节及以下）,旨在通过教育与文化交流增进美国人民与其他国家人民之间的相互理解。该法授权外国人参加美国境内多种交流访问者项目。《交流访问者项目条例》涵盖以下项目类别：教授和研究学者、短期学者、受训人员和实习生、大专院校学生、教师、中学生、专家、外籍医师、国际访问者、政府访问者、夏令营辅导员、互惠生以及暑期工作旅游人员。[41]
The J nonimmigrant classification was created in 1961 by the Mutual Educational and Cultural Exchange Act of 1961, also known as the Fulbright-Hays Act of 1961, Public Law 87-256, 75 Stat. 527 (22 U.S.C. 2451, et seq. ), to increase mutual understanding between the people of the United States and the people of other countries by means of educational and cultural exchanges. It authorizes aliens to participate in a variety of exchange visitor programs in the United States. The Exchange Visitor Program regulations cover the following program categories: professors and research scholars, short-term scholars, trainees and interns, college and university students, teachers, secondary school students, specialists, alien physicians, international visitors, government visitors, camp counselors, au pairs, and summer work travel.[41]
1985年以前,J类交流访问者获准的初始入境期限为其项目期限,最长不超过一年。[42] 1985年,相关法规被修订,允许J类交流访问者获准入境期限为其项目期限加30天。[43]这种从固定期限入境改为按在校期限(D/S)入境的变更,是持续努力减少公众报告要求以及减轻机构处理延期申请所带来的文书负担工作的一部分。[44]2020年曾提出对J类交流访问者的在校期限(D/S)作出修改,但该提案已于2021年撤回。[45]
Prior to 1985, J exchange visitors were granted an initial admission for the period of their program up to one year.[42] In 1985, the regulations were amended to allow J exchange visitors to be admitted for the duration of their program plus 30 days.[43] This change from being admitted for a fixed period to D/S was implemented as part of a continuing effort to reduce reporting requirements for the public as well as the paperwork burden on the agency associated with processing extension requests.[44] Changes to D/S were proposed for J exchange visitors in 2020, but the proposal was withdrawn in 2021.[45]
拟参加交流的访问者必须由美国国务院(DoS)指定的项目主办方担保,方可以J类非移民身份入境美国并参加交流访问者项目。美国国务院指定的主办方将向拟参加交流的访问者签发DS-2019表,即《交流访问者(J-1)身份资格证明书》。DS-2019表使拟参加交流的访问者得以在境外的美国使领馆申请J-1非移民签证,或在入境口岸(POE)申请以J-1非移民身份入境。J-1交流访问者入境美国的期限为在校期限(D/S),即其交流访问者项目的期限。[46]
A prospective exchange visitor must be sponsored by a DoS-designated program sponsor to be admitted to the United States in the J nonimmigrant classification and participate in an exchange visitor program. The DoS designated sponsor will issue a prospective J exchange visitor a Form DS-2019, Certificate of Eligibility for Exchange Visitor (J-1) Status. The DS-2019 permits a prospective exchange visitor to apply for a J-1 nonimmigrant visa at a U.S. embassy or consulate abroad or seek admission as a J-1 nonimmigrant at a POE. A J-1 exchange visitor is admitted into the United States for D/S, which is the length of his or her exchange visitor program.[46]
(印刷页44982)
( printed page 44982)
J类交流访问者项目的延期事宜受美国国务院法规管辖。[47]如有权限延长项目期限,交流访问者项目主办方的负责官员(RO)[48]（其角色类似于F-1学生情境中的指定校方负责人）有权通过签发正式签署的DS-2019表为J类交流访问者延长项目期限。[49]超出法规规定最长项目期限的延期申请,必须经美国国务院批准,由其裁定此类延期事宜。美国公民及移民服务局(USCIS)不裁定此类项目延期事宜；但是,USCIS确实裁定由其他非移民身份转换为J类身份的申请。如上所述,根据《非法移民改革和移民责任法》(IIRIRA)及《美国爱国者法案》(公法107-56号)的要求,J类交流访问者项目同样通过SEVIS系统进行监控。
Extensions of J exchange visitor programs are governed by DoS regulations.[47] If there is authority to extend a program, the exchange visitor program sponsor's RO,[48] similar to the DSO in the F-1 student context, is authorized to extend a J exchange visitor's program by issuing a duly executed Form DS-2019.[49] Requests for extensions beyond the maximum program duration provided in the regulations must be approved by DoS, which adjudicates these extensions. USCIS does not adjudicate these program extensions; however, USCIS does adjudicate requests to change into J status from another nonimmigrant status. As outlined above, consistent with the requirements in IIRIRA and the USA PATRIOT Act, Public Law 107-56, J exchange visitor programs are also monitored using SEVIS.
3. I类签证分类
3. I Classification
《移民与国籍法》(INA)第101(a)(15)(I)条将I类别定义为,在互惠的基础上,作为外国新闻、广播、电影或其他外国信息媒体的真实代表的外国人,其寻求入境美国的唯一目的是从事此类职业,以及该代表的配偶和子女,如与其同行或随后前来团聚。目前,大多数非移民信息媒体代表(持有中华人民共和国(PRC)签发护照者除外)获准在其受雇期间入境。在获得美国公民及移民服务局(USCIS)许可之前,他们不得变更其信息媒体或雇主。[50]
Section 101(a)(15)(I) of the INA defines the I classification as, upon a basis of reciprocity, an alien who is a bona fide representative of foreign press, radio, film, or other foreign information media who seeks to enter the United States solely to engage in such vocation, and the spouse and children of such a representative, if accompanying or following to join him or her. Most nonimmigrant representatives of information media (with the exception of those presenting a passport issued by the PRC) are currently admitted for the duration of their employment. They are not permitted to change their information medium or employer until they obtain permission from USCIS.[50]
从1973年到1985年,以I非移民身份获准进入美国的外国人获准的停留期限为1年,并可延期。[51] 1985年,原移民归化局(legacy INS)修订了相关法规,允许非移民信息媒体代表在其受雇期间获准入境。[52] 将I类非移民的入境期限从固定期限改为按受雇期限入境的这一变更,是为持续减少公众报告负担以及减轻该机构处理延期申请相关文书工作负担所作努力的一部分。[53] 通过对授权I类非移民按受雇期限入境相关法规的管理,美国国土安全部(DHS)目前对所有I类非移民均准予按受雇期限(D/S)入境,持有中华人民共和国(PRC)签发护照者除外(香港特别行政区(SAR)护照或澳门特别行政区护照持有人不受此限制)。[54] 2020年曾提议对I类外国媒体代表的D/S制度作出变更,但该提案已于2021年撤回。[55]
From 1973 to 1985, aliens admitted to the United States in I nonimmigrant status were admitted for a period of 1 year with the possibility of extensions.[51] In 1985, legacy INS amended the regulations to allow nonimmigrant representatives of information media to be admitted for the duration of their employment.[52] This change from a set time period of admission to admission for duration of employment for I nonimmigrants was implemented as part of a continuing effort to reduce reporting requirements for the public, as well as the paperwork burden associated with processing extension requests on the agency.[53] Through its administration of the regulations authorizing I nonimmigrants admission for duration of employment, DHS currently admits all I nonimmigrants for D/S, with the exception of those presenting a passport issued by the PRC (other than a Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) passport or a Macau SAR passport).[54] Changes to D/S were proposed for I foreign media representatives in 2020, but the proposal was withdrawn in 2021.[55]
C. 制定规则的必要性
C. Need for Rulemaking
1. 对F、J和I类非移民身份完整性的风险
1. Risks to the Integrity of the F, J, and I Nonimmigrant Classifications
美国国土安全部欢迎F类学术学生、J类交流访问学者和I类外国信息媒体代表,但也承认,由于相关人员数量庞大,监督和审查工作因而变得复杂。自1980年以来,获准进入美国的F类非移民学生人数增长了六倍以上。[56] 同样,自1985年对J类和I类非移民引入按受雇期限(D/S)入境制度以来,获准进入美国的交流访问学者人数增长了四倍以上,而外国信息媒体代表人数则增长了一倍以上。[57]
DHS welcomes F academic students, J exchange visitors, and I representatives of foreign information media, but it also acknowledges that the sheer size of the population complicates oversight and vetting functions. Since 1980, the number of F nonimmigrant students admitted into the United States has more than sextupled.[56] Similarly, since D/S was introduced for J and I nonimmigrants in 1985, the number of exchange visitors admitted into the United States has more than quadrupled while the number of representatives of foreign information media has more than doubled.[57]
美国国土安全部使用基于网络的系统SEVIS,维护以下相关信息:经学生及交流访问者项目(SEVP)认证的学校;在美国学习的F-1学生(及其F-2受抚养人);在美国就读职业课程的M-1学生(及其M-2受抚养人);经美国国务院(DoS)指定的交流访问者项目(Exchange Visitor Program)发起方;以及J-1交流访问者项目参与者(及其J-2受抚养人)。SEVIS系统对国家安全而言是必要的,并符合《非法移民改革和移民责任法》(IIRIRA)、《爱国者法案》(USA PATRIOT Act)以及《9/11委员会报告》中的相关要求。
DHS uses SEVIS, a web-based system, to maintain information regarding: SEVP-certified schools; F-1 students studying in the United States (and their F-2 dependents); M-1 students enrolled in vocational programs in the United States (and their M-2 dependents); DoS-designated Exchange Visitor Program sponsors; and J-1 Exchange Visitor Program participants (and their J-2 dependents). SEVIS is necessary for national security and is consistent with the requirements in IIRIRA, the USA PATRIOT Act, and the 9/11 Commission Report.
教育机构和项目发起方的雇员,特别是指定学校官员(DSO)和负责人(RO),在SEVIS系统中发挥着重要作用。他们负责监督学生和交流访问者,准确地将学生和交流访问者的活动信息录入SEVIS系统,并恰当地判定该学生或交流访问者的SEVIS记录应保持活跃状态,或因情况变化而需作出相应变更。[58] 在此框架下,学术学生或交流访问者通常通过遵守经DSO或RO认证的项目条件来维持合法身份。然而,项目延期与外国人非移民停留期限的延期是不同的概念。美国国土安全部认为,由DSO推荐学术项目延期、由RO推荐交流访问者项目延期是适当的;然而,停留期延期申请(EOS)涉及对外国人是否在法律上有资格以特定非移民身份延长其在美国的停留期限,以及其是否一直遵守其入境条款和条件的裁定。[59] 美国国土安全部认为,项目延期的认定与停留期延期申请(EOS)的认定应当加以区分(第44983页),DSO和RO的推荐意见应作为移民官员在审核停留期延期申请时所考量的因素之一。将入境期限改为固定期限,将为移民官员提供一种机制,使其能够以合理且频繁的间隔进行此类评估。
Employees of educational institutions and program sponsors, specifically DSOs and ROs, play a large role in SEVIS. They are responsible for monitoring students and exchange visitors, accurately entering information about the students' and exchange visitors' activities into SEVIS, and properly determining whether the student or exchange visitor's SEVIS record should remain in active status or change to reflect a change in circumstances.[58] Under this framework, an academic student or exchange visitor generally maintains lawful status by complying with the conditions of the program, as certified by the DSO or RO. However, a program extension and an extension of an alien's nonimmigrant stay are different. DHS believes it is appropriate for the DSO to recommend an extension of an academic program and an RO to recommend an extension of an exchange visitor program; however, an EOS involves an adjudication of whether an alien is legally eligible to extend his or her stay in the United States in a given nonimmigrant status and has been complying with the terms and conditions of his or her admission.[59] DHS believes that the determinations of program extension and EOS should be ( printed page 44983) separated, with the DSO's and RO's recommendation being one factor an immigration officer reviews while adjudicating an application for EOS. Changing to a fixed period of admission will give immigration officers a mechanism to make this evaluation at reasonably frequent intervals.
此外，国土安全部（DHS）预计这一变更将遏制和防止欺诈行为，因为要求直接向移民官员报到，从本质上说，很可能会遏制对F类和J类非移民身份中被认为存在的漏洞的利用行为。直接评估、改善记录保存和防止欺诈所带来的同样益处，也将适用于I类人员。
Additionally, DHS expects this change will deter and prevent fraud, as a requirement to check in directly with an immigration officer is inherently likely to deter exploitation of perceived vulnerabilities in the F and J nonimmigrant classifications. The same benefits of direct evaluation, better recordkeeping, and fraud prevention will also apply to the I population.
2. F类身份中存在的风险
2. Risks Within the F Classification
国土安全部（DHS）意识到F-1项目存在欺诈、利用和滥用的问题。自2008年以来，多名学校业主及其他人员因“付费滞留”欺诈行为而受到刑事起诉，在此类欺诈中，学校官员为收取现金报酬，虚假报告未实际到校就读的F-1学生仍在维持其学生身份。[60]在某些案件中，被定罪的学校业主经营多所学校，并在学校之间转移学生以掩盖欺诈行为。[61]国土安全部还担心这些学校的指定学校官员（DSO）参与了这些滥用行为，部分指定学校官员故意不准确地记录学生的身份状态。[62]此外，指定学校官员曾向那些没有令人信服的医疗或学业理由而未能在规定结业日期前完成学业的学生发放项目延期，国土安全部仍持续观察到F-1学生长期在学校注册就读的情况。例如，国土安全部此前在《拟议规则制定通知》（NPRM）中指出一名非移民案例，该人自1991年至2021年作为F-1学生就读于一所舞蹈学校。尽管该舞蹈课程的正常学制据报为5年，但该校在2003年（启用学生和交流访问者信息系统SEVIS成为强制要求之时）至2020年间，共批准了17次项目延期，声称该学生需要更多时间，尽管其注册时间已近30年。该学生随后转入另一所学校的英语培训项目，该项目开课日期为2022年11月，尽管此时她作为F-1学生在美国已停留超过30年。她在该校注册至2025年12月，随后转入另一所学校开始新的语言培训，项目开课日期为2026年1月19日，项目结业日期为2029年1月19日。她作为F-1学生的身份已持续约35年。若她在该校就读至当前规定的结业日期，她将在美国以F-1身份停留近38年。[63]在另一起案件中，国土安全部还发现一名非移民自2008年4月21日开始的英语培训项目起，已持续F-1学生身份超过18年。他先后注册了四个语言培训项目、四个学士学位项目，目前正在攻读神学/神学研究硕士学位项目，项目结业日期为2027年8月。[64]另一名学生自2009年至2020年在同一所学校注册就读，自2005年起即为F-1学生，共获得14次项目延期批准。国土安全部还发现三名攻读博士学位的F-1学生，其完成学业所用时间超过20年，另有5名在社区学院就读副学士学位项目的F-1学生，其注册时长超过5年，其中部分长达十年之久。[65]此外，也存在部分指定学校官员允许未能维持身份的学生转学至另一所学校，而非要求其申请身份恢复的案例。[66]除国土安全部和美国司法部（DOJ）公开认定的案件外，国土安全部还担忧存在指定学校官员未察觉学生身份违规情况的案件。
DHS is aware that the F-1 program is subject to fraud, exploitation, and abuse. Since 2008, multiple school owners and others have been criminally prosecuted for “pay-to-stay” fraud, in which school officials, in return for cash payments, falsely report that F-1 students who do not attend school are maintaining their student status.[60] In some cases, convicted school owners operated multiple schools and transferred students among them to conceal the fraud.[61] DHS is also concerned that DSOs at these schools were complicit in these abuses; some DSOs intentionally recorded a student's status inaccurately.[62] Further, DSOs have issued program extensions to students who did not have compelling medical or academic reasons for failing to complete their program by its end date and DHS continues to observe F-1 students enrolling in schools for extended periods of time. For example, DHS previously identified in the NPRM a nonimmigrant who was an F-1 student at a dance school from 1991-2021. Although the reported normal length of the dance program is 5 years, the school issued 17 program extensions between 2003 (when the use of SEVIS was mandated) and 2020, claiming that the student needed more time despite nearly 30 years of enrollment. The student subsequently transferred to an English language training program at another school with a program start date in November 2022, despite more than 30 years in the United States as an F-1 student. She remained enrolled there until December 2025, when she transferred to another school to commence additional language training with a program start date of January 19, 2026, and a program end date of January 19, 2029. She has been an F-1 student for approximately 35 years. If she remains at the school through the current program end date, she will have spent nearly 38 years in the United States in F-1 status.[63] In another case, DHS also identified a nonimmigrant who has been in F-1 student status for more than 18 years since he enrolled in an English language training program that began on April 21, 2008. He has enrolled in four language training programs, four bachelor's programs, and is currently enrolled in a master's in theology/theological studies program with a program end date in August 2027.[64] Another student who was enrolled at the same school from 2009 to 2020 and had been an F-1 student since 2005, was granted 14 program extensions. DHS also identified three F-1 students in doctoral programs that have taken over 20 years to complete their programs, and 5 F-1 students at community colleges have been enrolled in associate degree programs for periods in excess of 5 years—some for as long as a decade.[65] There are also examples where some DSOs permitted students who failed to maintain status to transfer to another school rather than apply for reinstatement.[66] Beyond cases publicly identified by DHS and the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ), DHS is concerned about cases where DSOs were not aware of status violations by students.
除了对参与欺诈计划的指定学校官员(DSO)和学校所有者的担忧外,国土安全部(DHS)也对外国人自身的行为感到担忧。一些外国人利用F类签证身份,通过持续注册或在学校之间转学,在美国居留长达数十年,这种做法因在读状态(D/S)框架而更易实现。[67] 国土安全部已识别出超过2,100名于2000年至2010年间首次以F-1学生身份入境、且截至2025年4月6日仍保持有效F-1身份的外国人。[68] 为延长其停留期限,这些外国人连续注册多个教育项目,反复转学至新学校,或由指定学校官员反复延长其项目结束日期。这种做法并不局限于某一特定类型的学校;社区学院或初级学院、大学以及语言培训学校的学生均存在长期维持F-1身份的情况。国土安全部对此类长期停留情形是否违反相关法律的立法本意表示担忧,因为学生身份本应是临时性的,外国人不得有放弃其在外国居所的意图,且其主要目的应为学习,而非作为无限期留在美国的手段。[69](印刷页44984)
Apart from concerns about DSOs and school owners involved in fraudulent schemes, DHS also has concerns about the actions of the aliens themselves. Some aliens have used the F classification to reside in the United States for decades by continuously enrolling in or transferring between schools, a practice facilitated by the D/S framework.[67] DHS identified over 2,100 aliens who first entered as F-1 students between 2000 and 2010 and remain in active F-1 status as of April 6, 2025.[68] To extend their stay, these aliens enrolled in consecutive educational programs, repeatedly transferred to new schools, or DSOs repeatedly extended their program end dates. This practice is not limited to any one particular type of school; students at community or junior colleges, universities, and language training schools have maintained F-1 status for lengthy periods. DHS is concerned that such instances of extended stays may violate the underlying statutory intent given that student status is meant to be temporary, with the alien having no intention of abandoning their residence in a foreign country, and for the primary purpose of studying, not as a way to ( printed page 44984) remain in the United States indefinitely.[69]
利用F类签证身份在美国居留长达数十年,令人对该外国人是否确实意图按照《移民与国籍法》(INA)要求仅临时停留美国产生怀疑。[70] 这也引发了对这些外国人是否为真正善意的非移民学生、是否通过遵守其入境条件(包括仅从事全日制学习并取得课程进展)来维持合法有效身份的担忧。同样,这也令人对这些外国人是否确实拥有足够的经济资源支付学费和生活费用,而无需从事未经授权的工作产生疑问。
The use of the F classification to remain in the United States for decades raises doubts that the alien's intention was to stay in the United States temporarily, as required by the INA.[70] It also raises concerns as to whether those aliens are bona fide nonimmigrant students who are maintaining valid lawful status by complying with the terms of their admission, which include solely pursuing a full course of study and progressing to completing a course of study. Likewise, it raises concerns as to whether these aliens truly have the financial resources to cover tuition and living expenses without engaging in unauthorized employment.
即使在选择性实习培训(OPT)等项目下获得工作授权的情况下,国土安全部也发现存在欺诈行为,使学生能够在美国停留而实际上并未从事合法工作。移民及海关执法局(ICE)代理局长Todd Lyons于2026年5月12日的新闻发布会上向记者表示,ICE已识别出逾10,000起与OPT项目相关的潜在欺诈案件。这些案件是在实地走访及其他调查手段显示部分雇主仅为空壳公司后被发现的,这些空壳公司帮助应届毕业生在未在合法美国公司实际工作的情况下留在美国,或为名义上设在美国、实际由境外管理的公司工作,此举违反了要求接受美国境内培训与指导的法律规定。[71]
Even when employment is authorized under programs such as the Optional Practical Training (OPT), DHS has found fraud that enabled students to stay in the U.S. without actually having legitimate jobs. ICE Acting Director Todd Lyons told reporters at a press conference on May 12, 2026, that ICE had identified more than 10,000 cases of potential fraud associated with the OPT program. The cases were identified after site visits and other investigative techniques showed that some employers were just shell companies helping recent graduates stay in the U.S. without actual work at a legitimate U.S. company or working for supposedly U.S. based companies managed from abroad, which violates the law requiring U.S. training and direction.[71]
此外,尽管一些学校所有者和学校高管已因违反法律而承担法律后果,但根据《移民与国籍法》第212(a)(9)(B)条和第(C)条(8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(9)(B)和(C))规定,以在读状态(D/S)获准入境的非移民通常不会为三年和十年禁止入境期之目的而累积非法居留时间,除非移民官员在裁决移民福利申请时认定其违反身份,或移民法官裁定将其排除出境、驱逐出境或遣返。[72] 由于F-1学生以在读状态(D/S)获准入境,他们通常无需向美国公民及移民服务局(USCIS)提交诸如延长停留期限(EOS)申请等申请或请愿书,因此,移民官员通常没有机会确定这些学生是否正在从事F-1非移民活动以及是否维持其F-1非移民身份。
Further, while some school owners and school executives have faced legal consequences for their violation of the law, nonimmigrants admitted for D/S generally do not accrue unlawful presence for purposes of the 3- and 10-year bars described in INA 212(a)(9)(B) and (C), 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(9)(B) and (C), unless an immigration officer finds they have violated their status in the context of adjudicating an immigration benefit request, or an immigration judge orders them excluded, deported, or removed.[72] Because F-1 students are admitted for D/S, they generally do not file applications or petitions, such as EOS applications, with USCIS, and therefore, immigration officers do not generally have an opportunity to determine whether the students are engaging in F-1 nonimmigrant activities in the United States and maintaining their F-1 nonimmigrant status.
美国政府问责局(GAO)已就国土安全部(DHS)对指定校方代表(DSO)和非移民学生的担忧进行了报告。2019年,GAO和美国移民及海关执法局(ICE)发布了一份报告,指出了与管理学校重新认证和项目培训相关的学生及交流访问学者项目(SEVP)欺诈风险。该报告包括了与让学校所有者和DSO参与监督F-1学生维持身份有关的脆弱性。[73]在该报告中,GAO指出了学生和学校双方的欺诈脆弱性。例如,学生声称维持身份但实际并未维持,如未出勤上课或从事未经授权的工作,又或学校所有者未要求已注册学生出勤上课,或为不符合学术项目资格的学生制作虚假文件。GAO建议ICE制定欺诈风险概况,并使用数据分析来识别申请认证的学校中的潜在欺诈指标,制定并实施针对DSO的欺诈培训,并加强对DSO的背景审查。[74]
The U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) has reported on DHS's concerns about DSOs and nonimmigrant students. In 2019, GAO and ICE published a report identifying fraud risks to SEVP related to managing school recertification and program training. The report included vulnerabilities associated with involving school owners and DSOs in overseeing the maintenance of status of F-1 students.[73] In the report, GAO identified fraud vulnerabilities on the part of both students and schools. Examples include students claiming to maintain status when they are not, such as failing to attend class or working without appropriate authorization, or school owners not requiring enrolled students to attend classes or creating fraudulent documentation for students who are ineligible for the academic program. GAO recommended that ICE develop a fraud risk profile and use data analytics to identify potential fraud indicators in schools petitioning for certification, develop and implement fraud training for DSOs, and strengthen background checks for DSOs.[74]
国土安全部认为,本规则可通过将F类非移民的获准入境期限和延期期限设定为该F类非移民特定项目的时长(但不超过4年期限),在一定程度上减轻欺诈风险。本规则将建立一种机制,使移民官员能够在规定的时间节点(例如在4年入境期限届满后于美国境内申请延长居留期(EOS)时)对这些非移民进行评估,并确定其是否遵守其身份分类的条件。移民官员在获得国土安全部授权执行国家移民法律之前,须接受背景审查、安全许可和培训,这包括在审理申请时评估非移民是否符合延长居留的要求,学生是否在DSO不知情的情况下违反了其非移民身份,或DSO是否通过不要求学生上课或伪造文件而从事欺诈行为。移民官员还接受了评估申请中欺诈迹象的培训,并进行审查和审核,这可能有助于发现欺诈或滥用行为。这将为国土安全部提供进一步的机会,以识别并追究违反F-1身份的外国人及其教育机构的责任。国土安全部目前采用8 CFR 214.3(h)条所规定的对经SEVP认证学校的周期外审查和重新认证措施,以确保学校遵守有关记录保存和报告要求的规定。国土安全部也可随时对学校进行实地审查,如发现不合规或违反法规的情况,可能导致撤销SEVP认证。在现行的“持续期限”(D/S)框架下,如果学生持续在校注册、不寻求重新入境美国且不申请其他移民福利,国土安全部可能在很长一段时间内都无法发现个别F-1身份违规行为。如果国土安全部定期进行评估以核实F-1学生是否维持其学生身份,国土安全部便能更好地发现并减少此类违规行为以及其所在学校的违规行为。[75]如果这些非移民希望在其固定入境期限届满后继续留在美国,本规则将为此类审查创造机会。这也可能产生威慑效果,使那些原本打算来到美国(第44985页)从事上述部分行为、并认为可在长时间内不被发现的人望而却步。国土安全部认为,这是维护美国移民体系完整性的更为适当的方式。此外,国土安全部认为,这些变化将使移民官员能够直接核实,申请延长居留期(EOS)的学生除其他事项外:是否拥有足够资金在美国生活和学习而无需从事未经授权的工作;是否在国外保持住所并有意返回该住所;是否已经并正在修读全日制课程;以及是否在与其在美国的高等教育项目相关的通常适用的4年期限内完成学业,或能否就需要更长时间完成学业提供可允许的说明。
DHS believes it can mitigate fraud risks in this rule in part through setting the authorized admission and extension periods for F nonimmigrants as the length of the F nonimmigrant's specific program, not to exceed a 4-year period. The rule will establish a mechanism for immigration officers to assess these nonimmigrants at defined periods (such as when applying for an EOS in the United States beyond a 4-year admission period) and determine whether they are complying with the conditions of their classification. Immigration officers receive background checks, clearances, and training before DHS authorizes them to implement the nation's immigration laws, which includes as part of adjudicating the application whether nonimmigrants meet the requirements to extend their stay, whether a student has violated his or her nonimmigrant status without the DSO's awareness or whether DSOs are engaging in fraud by not requiring students to attend classes or by falsifying documents. Immigration officers are further trained to assess applications for fraud indicators and conduct reviews and vetting that may assist in the detection of fraud or abuse. This will provide further opportunities for DHS to identify and hold accountable aliens who violate their F-1 status, as well as their educational institutions. DHS currently employs out-of-cycle reviews and recertification of SEVP-certified schools outlined in 8 CFR 214.3(h) to ensure the school's compliance with regulatory recordkeeping and reporting requirements. DHS may also conduct on-site reviews of schools at any time, which may lead to withdrawal of SEVP certification upon findings of noncompliance or regulatory violations. Under the current D/S framework, DHS might not detect an individual F-1 status violation for an extended period if the student stays enrolled in a school, does not seek readmission to the United States, and does not apply for additional immigration benefits. If DHS makes periodic assessments to verify that F-1 students are maintaining their student status, DHS could better detect and mitigate against these violations as well as violations by their school.[75] The rule creates opportunities for this scrutiny if these nonimmigrants wish to remain beyond their fixed period of admission. This may also have the effect of deterring individuals who would otherwise seek to come to the United ( printed page 44985) States and engage in some of the behaviors discussed above, believing they would be able to do so undetected for long periods of time. DHS believes this is a more appropriate way to maintain the integrity of the U.S. immigration system. Additionally, DHS believes the changes will allow immigration officers to directly verify, among other things, that students applying for an EOS: have the funds needed to live and study in the United States without engaging in unauthorized work; are maintaining a residence abroad to which they intend to return; have pursued and are pursuing a full course of study; and are completing their studies within the 4-year generally applicable timeframe relating to their post-secondary education programs in the United States or are able to provide a permissible explanation for taking a longer period of time to complete the program.
最后,由于“在读状态”（D/S）框架减少了移民官员对外国留学生进行直接审查的机会,这为外国对手利用F-1项目、破坏美国国家安全创造了可乘之机。在D/S框架下,美国国土安全部（DHS）已在F-1项目中发现了国家安全威胁。例如,2023年3月24日,一名俄罗斯男子被指控充当外国政府代理人、签证欺诈、银行欺诈、电信欺诈及其他罪名,这些指控源于其在美国作为俄罗斯情报机构“非法”代理人从事非法活动。他于2018年以假冒的巴西身份获得F-1签证,并利用该签证进入美国,于2018年至2020年期间就读于一所美国大学。[76]近年来,多名F-1学生因涉及与美国军事基地有关的非法活动而被捕。[77]2024年1月18日,美国联邦调查局（FBI）逮捕了一名来自中国的学生,罪名为非法操作无人机系统、违反国防空域规定以及拍摄国防设施照片,此前调查发现该学生使用商用无人机对位于弗吉尼亚州诺福克地区的美国海军基地进行了拍照。美国弗吉尼亚州东区联邦地方法院纽波特纽斯分院于2024年10月2日判决其未经授权使用飞行器对指定设施进行非法拍摄罪名成立,他于2025年5月7日被驱逐出境。[78]2020年6月,三名中国公民因非法拍摄位于佛罗里达州基韦斯特的一处美国海军设施被判处联邦监禁。被捕者中两人为F-1学生,一人为J-1交流访问者。[79]2024年10月,五名中国学生因在2023年8月于密歇根州格雷林营地举行的一次有数千名军方官员（其中包括部分来自台湾的人员）参加的训练演习期间被发现持有相机,而被指控共谋、作虚假陈述及销毁记录,此案与一项联邦调查有关。[80]上述每一个案例均为DHS于2026年6月2日对学生和交流访问者信息系统（SEVIS）数据进行分析所得。
Finally, because the D/S framework reduces opportunities for direct vetting of foreign academic students by immigration officers, it creates opportunities for foreign adversaries to exploit the F-1 program and undermine U.S. national security. Under the D/S framework, DHS has identified national security threats within the F-1 program. For example, on March 24, 2023, a Russian man was charged with acting as an agent of a foreign power, visa fraud, bank fraud, wire fraud, and other charges stemming from his illegal activities in the United States functioning as an “illegal” agent for a Russian Intelligence Service. He obtained an F-1 visa in 2018 under an assumed Brazilian identity, which he used to enter the United States and enroll in a U.S. university from 2018 to 2020.[76] In recent years, multiple F-1 students have been arrested in connection with illegal activities pertaining to U.S. military bases.[77] On January 18, 2024 the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) arrested a student from China for prohibited operation of an unmanned aircraft system, violation of national defense airspace, and photography of defense installations after an investigation revealed the student utilized a commercial drone to take photographs of U.S. naval bases in the Norfolk, Virginia area. The U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia's Newport News Division convicted him for use of an aircraft for the unlawful photographing of designated installation without authorization on October 2, 2024, and he was removed from the United States on May 7, 2025.[78] In June 2020, three Chinese nationals were sentenced to federal prison for illegal photography of a U.S. naval installation in Key West, Florida. Two of those arrested were F-1 students, and one was a J-1 exchange visitor.[79] In October 2024, five Chinese students were charged with conspiracy, making false statements and destroying records in connection with a federal investigation after they were observed with cameras at Camp Grayling in Michigan during a training exercise in August 2023 where thousands of military officials, including some from Taiwan, were participating.[80] Each of these examples was part of DHS's analysis of SEVIS data on June 2, 2026.
除对国家安全构成风险外,部分F-1学生还对公共安全构成风险,并曾因犯罪行为被起诉。DHS已查明,自2024年以来,有多名F-1学生因参与针对美国境内弱势群体及老年受害者的复杂金融诈骗活动而被捕。其中部分诈骗计划造成受害者损失高达数十万美元。在某些案例中,多名F-1学生因参与同一诈骗计划而被捕。[81]
In addition to creating risks to national security, some F-1 students pose risks to public safety and have been charged with criminal acts. DHS has identified multiple F-1 students arrested since 2024 for their roles in sophisticated financial scams targeting vulnerable and elderly victims in the United States. Some of these schemes resulted in hundreds of thousands of dollars in losses to victims. In some instances, multiple F-1 students were arrested for their involvement in the same schemes.[81]
美国开放的教育环境固然带来益处,但也使研究型大学及国家面临外国学生从事经济、学术或军事间谍活动的风险。外国对手正日益采用愈加复杂和具有资源优势的手段,利用美国的教育环境,其中包括若干有据可查的通过学生项目实施间谍活动的案例。[82]（印刷页44986）要发现并遏制对手利用F-1项目对美国国家安全构成的新兴威胁,需要加强监管。2022年,美国政府问责局（GAO）应国会询问展开调查,并建议美国移民及海关执法局（ICE）修改SEVIS系统,纳入可能表明哪些外国学生或学者在美国大学中存在较高技术转让风险的相关因素。[83]
An open education environment in the United States offers benefits, but it also places research universities and the nation at risk for economic, academic, or military espionage by foreign students. Foreign adversaries are using progressively sophisticated and resourceful methods to exploit the U.S. educational environment, including well-documented cases of espionage through the student program. [82] ( printed page 44986) Detecting and deterring emerging threats to U.S. national security posed by adversaries exploiting the F-1 program requires additional oversight. In 2022, in response to a Congressional inquiry, GAO investigated and made recommendations that ICE modify the SEVIS system to include factors that potentially indicate which foreign students or scholars may pose more risk of transferring technology at U.S. universities.[83]
国土安全部(DHS)认为,以固定期限的入境期替代F-1学生的‘在本国境内停留期限’(D/S)入境方式,将有助于缓解这些国家安全风险,其做法是确保由移民官员直接且定期地审查延长居留申请人,并借此确认其仅从事与其学生身份相符的活动。申请延长居留期限(EOS)的F-1非移民还必须证明其具备可入境资格,未能证明者将导致延长居留申请被拒绝。可入境资格的认定事项十分复杂,应当由受过专业训练的国土安全部官员进行评估。目前,当F-1非移民向其所在院校申请延长课程时,并未进行此类评估。[84] 值得注意的是,根据对F类非移民入境期限及相应延长居留申请程序的修改,国土安全部可以更频繁地从F类非移民学生处采集生物特征信息及其他信息(例如证明其有足够经济来源支付费用的证据,以及任何犯罪活动的证据),从而加强政府对此类外国人的监督与监测。
DHS believes that replacing admissions for D/S for F-1 students with admission for a fixed time period will help mitigate these national security risks by ensuring an immigration official directly and periodically vets applicants for extensions of stay and, in so doing, confirms they are engaged only in activities consistent with their student status. F-1 nonimmigrants applying for EOS will also be required to establish they are admissible, and failure to do so will result in denial of the EOS. Admissibility grounds are complex and are properly assessed by a trained DHS officer. Such an assessment is not currently made when F-1 nonimmigrants apply for an extension of their program with their institution.[84] Significantly, under the changes to the period of admission of F nonimmigrants and the applicable EOS process, DHS may collect biometrics and other information (such as evidence of financial resources to cover expenses and evidence of any criminal activity) from F nonimmigrant students more frequently, thereby enhancing the Government's oversight and monitoring of these aliens.
三、J类签证中存在的风险
3. Risks Within the J Classification
国土安全部认为,持J类签证的个人以‘在本国境内停留期限’(D/S)方式入境所带来的国家安全风险,与F类签证所带来的风险相似。[85] 根据美国国立卫生研究院(NIH)于2018年12月委托一个专家小组就联邦资助科研活动中的外国影响问题所作的研究报告,“少数科学家严重违反了美国国立卫生研究院的政策与制度规定,未披露其在其他国家获得的外国资助(即资助款项)、实验室或受资助的教职职位。”[86] 与F类非移民的情形相同,将J类非移民具体项目的期限设定为不超过4年,将为移民官员提供一个在固定期限内(例如在4年入境期限届满后申请延长居留期限时)对该类非移民进行评估的机制,以判断其是否遵守了其签证类别的相关条件。这将加强对J类非移民群体的审查,有助于防范和震慑心怀不轨者。
DHS believes that the national security risks posed by D/S admissions for individuals admitted under the J classification are similar to those posed by the F classification.[85] According to a December 2018 report by a panel of experts commissioned by the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to study foreign influence on federally-funded scientific research, “Small numbers of scientists have committed serious violations of NIH policies and systems by not disclosing foreign support ( i.e., grants), laboratories, or funded faculty positions in other countries.” [86] As with F nonimmigrants, setting the length of the J nonimmigrant's specific program to not exceed a 4-year period will establish a mechanism for immigration officers to assess these nonimmigrants at defined periods (such as when applying for an EOS in the United States beyond a 4-year admission period) and determine whether they are complying with the conditions of their classification. This will increase vetting of the J nonimmigrant population, which can help to prevent and deter nefarious actors.
有多个实例表明,在‘在本国境内停留期限’(D/S)框架下,J类非移民持续构成国家安全威胁,这进一步证明了加强该项目监管的必要性。例如,2009年,一名伊朗籍公民获签发J-1签证,于2009年9月至2010年8月期间在美国一所大学担任计算机科学客座教授。2012年11月8日,美国财政部外国资产管制办公室(“OFAC”)根据2012年10月9日第13628号行政命令《授权实施〈2012年伊朗威胁削减与叙利亚人权法〉所规定的若干制裁措施及对伊朗采取的额外制裁措施》,将其列为财产及财产权益被冻结人员。[87] 据报道,截至2009年2月,此人一直试图从境外获取与监控短信服务(SMS)通信相关的设备,且截至2012年7月初,他一直在积极协助伊朗政府开展互联网审查活动。[88] 2025年11月5日,三名来自中国的J-1研究学者被指控共谋将生物材料走私入境美国,并向美国海关与边境保护局(CBP)官员作虚假陈述。[89] 2025年6月,美国司法部宣布,两名中国籍J-1交流访问者因在美国一所大学实验室工作期间共谋将危险生物病原体走私入境美国而被指控。[90] 2025年11月5日,其中一名J-1交流访问者就将生物病原体走私入境美国并就此事向联邦调查局(FBI)探员说谎的指控认罪。[91]
There are multiple examples of ongoing national security threats posed by J nonimmigrants under the D/S framework, thereby supporting the need for increased oversight within the program. For example, in 2009, an Iranian national was issued a J-1 visa to be a visiting professor in computer science at a U.S. university from September 2009 to August 2010. On November 8, 2012, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (“OFAC”) designated him as a person whose property and interests in property are blocked pursuant to Executive Order 13628 of October 9, 2012, “Authorizing the Implementation of Certain Sanctions Set Forth in the Iran Threat Reduction and Syria Human Rights Act of 2012 and Additional Sanctions With Respect to Iran.” [87] He was reportedly attempting to acquire equipment related to the monitoring of Short Message Service (SMS) traffic from abroad as of February 2009 and, as of early July 2012, was actively assisting the Government of Iran's internet censorship activities.[88] On November 5, 2025, three J-1 research scholars from China were charged with conspiracy to smuggle biological materials into the United States and for making false statements to U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers.[89] In June 2025, the U.S. Department of Justice announced that two Chinese national J-1 exchange visitors were charged with conspiracy and smuggling a dangerous biological pathogen into the U.S. for their work at a U.S. university laboratory.[90] On November 5, 2025, one of the J-1 exchange visitors pleaded guilty to charges of smuggling a biological pathogen into the U.S. and then lying to FBI agents about it.[91]
另一个例证是,2019年9月,联邦调查局指控中国政府官员刘中三(音译,Zhongsan Liu)共谋以欺诈手段为多名中国官员骗取美国研究学者签证,而这些官员的真实目的是为中国境内的高科技开发项目招募美国科学家,这一事件生动展示了国家支持下非法获取美国技术的行为。[92] 刘中三被判犯有(印刷页第44987页)共谋欺骗美国政府及以欺诈手段获取美国签证罪。[93]
In another example, in September 2019, a stark illustration of state-sponsored efforts to illegally obtain United States technology emerged when the FBI charged Chinese government official Zhongsan Liu with conspiracy to fraudulently procure United States research scholar visas for Chinese officials whose actual purpose was to recruit United States scientists for high technology development programs within China.[92] Liu was convicted of ( printed page 44987) participating in conspiracy to defraud the United States and fraudulently obtain U.S. visas.[93]
此外,2019年12月,一名29岁的J-1身份研究生郑灶松(Zaosong Zheng)在哈佛大学参加交流访问学者项目期间,在波士顿洛根国际机场被拦截。联邦探员在其托运行李的一只袜子中发现用塑料袋包裹的21瓶棕色液体后,认定他属于“可能出口未申报生物材料的高风险人员”;打印和手写的笔记显示,“[该交流访问者]……正在故意收集和搜集知识产权……可能是代表中国政府。”[94]郑灶松因一项从美国走私货物罪和一项作出虚假、虚构或欺诈性陈述罪被起诉。
Additionally, in December 2019, Zaosong Zheng, a 29-year-old graduate student in J-1 status participating in an exchange visitor program at Harvard University, was stopped at Boston Logan International Airport. Federal agents determined he was a “high risk for possibly exporting undeclared biological material” after finding 21 vials of brown liquid wrapped in a plastic bag inside a sock in his checked luggage; typed and handwritten notes indicated “that [the exchange visitor] . . . was knowingly gathering and collecting intellectual property. . . possibly on behalf of the Chinese government.” [94] Zheng was indicted on one count of smuggling goods from the United States and one count of making false, fictitious or fraudulent statements.
2020年1月,叶琰青(Yanqing Ye)因在其J-1签证申请中谎称自己为“学生”,并隐瞒其在由中国共产党领导的一所顶尖军事院校中持续服役的军职身份,而被指控犯有签证欺诈罪、作出虚假陈述罪、充当外国政府代理人罪以及共谋罪,各一项。进一步指控称,在波士顿大学物理、化学与生物医学工程系学习期间,叶继续以中国人民解放军中尉身份任职,完成了解放军军官交办的多项任务,包括开展研究、评估美国军事网站,以及向中国发送美国文件和信息。[95]
In January 2020, Yanqing Ye was charged with one count each of visa fraud, making false statements, acting as an agent of a foreign government and conspiracy after Ye falsely identified herself on her J-1 visa application as a “student” and lied about her ongoing military service at a top military academy directed by the Chinese Communist Party. It was further alleged that while studying at Boston University's Department of Physics, Chemistry, and Biomedical Engineering, Ye continued to work as a People's Liberation Army Lieutenant completing numerous assignments from People's Liberation Army officers such as conducting research, assessing United States military websites and sending United States documents and information to China.[95]
2020年6月,一名持J-1签证进入美国在加州大学旧金山分校从事研究工作的中国公民,在洛杉矶国际机场试图返回中国时被捕,并被控犯有签证欺诈罪。根据法庭文件,他被指控系中华人民共和国人民解放军军官,并在其签证申请中就其军事服役情况提供了欺诈性信息。据称,他曾被其军事实验室主管指示将加州大学旧金山分校实验室的相关信息带回中国。[96]
In June 2020, a Chinese national who entered the United States on a J-1 visa to conduct research at the University of California, San Francisco was arrested at Los Angeles International Airport while attempting to return to China and charged with visa fraud. According to court documents, he allegedly is an officer with the PRC People's Liberation Army and provided fraudulent information about his military service in his visa application. He allegedly was instructed by his military lab supervisor to bring information back to China about the lab at University of California, San Francisco.[96]
2025年,密歇根大学一名J-1中国研究学者因共谋罪、向美国走私货物罪、虚假陈述罪和签证欺诈罪被刑事诉状起诉。联邦调查局(FBI)以涉嫌走私一种有害真菌为由逮捕了该交流访问学者,该真菌每年在全球造成数十亿美元的经济损失,并对人类和牲畜健康均造成危害。据称,该J-1签证持有人就其对该病原体的研究工作获得了中国政府资助,并且是中国共产党的忠实党员。[97]
In 2025, a J-1 Chinese research scholar at the University of Michigan was charged in a criminal complaint for conspiracy, smuggling goods into the United States, false statements, and visa fraud. The FBI arrested the exchange visitor for allegedly smuggling a noxious fungus which is responsible for billions of dollars in economic losses worldwide each year and causes health problems for both humans and livestock. The J-1 allegedly received Chinese government funding for her work on this pathogen and is a loyal member of the Chinese Communist Party.[97]
与F类非移民签证类似,国土安全部认为,将J-1签证持有人的“在美逗留期限”(D/S)许可改为固定期限入境许可,将有助于缓解上文所述的国家安全问题。交流访问者项目类别包括高等院校学生,这与F-1非移民身份具有相似之处。参加此类项目的学生与F-1非移民一样,从事中学后教育阶段的学习。参加学位项目的J-1高等院校学生,只要满足参与期限的相关要求,包括修读全日制课程,即可获准参加交流访问者项目,这与F-1非移民的全日制课程要求相呼应。J-1交流访问者的项目也可由责任官员(RO)延长,但须受国务院的监管和(或)批准,且无需向国土安全部提出申请。这些相似之处引发了与上文所述F-1签证相同的国家安全方面的担忧,以及对J-1签证持有人及其责任官员可能存在欺诈和滥用行为的担忧。通过对F-1和J-1实行相同的固定入境期限,交流访问者项目中的J-1高等院校学生将无法规避本规则的立法意图,[98]该意图旨在维护这些项目的完整性,并提供额外的保护措施和监督机制。由于J类交流访问者同样在学生及交流访问者信息系统(SEVIS)中被追踪记录,国土安全部认为,由移民官员定期确认外国人是否已妥善维持其身份,比依赖责任官员对J-1是否从事交流访问者项目所允许活动的核查更为有效。如上文所述,国土安全部认为,由移民官员裁定是否维持非移民身份以及外国人是否符合延长入境期限的资格更为妥当,因为这些官员经过了美国政府的背景审查、安全许可和培训。将“在美逗留期限”许可改为固定期限入境许可,将使移民官员有机会判定外国人是否符合延长期限的资格。如果官员在审理外国人的申请时发现其违反身份规定,其后果可能是立即产生的。延期居留(EOS)申请人还必须证明其具备入境许可资格,若未能证明,将导致延期居留申请被拒绝。[99]入境许可资格的认定较为复杂,应由经过培训的国土安全部官员妥善评估。目前,当J类交流访问者向其责任官员申请延长项目时,并不会进行此类评估。[100]因此,以固定期限而非“在美逗留期限”许可的方式准许J类交流访问者入境,将使国土安全部有更频繁的机会直接审查这些外国访问者,确保他们是真实的交流访问者,并能够预防和威慑J类交流访问者群体中的不法分子。根据对J类交流访问者入境期限及相应延期居留申请程序的变更,国土安全部可以更频繁地采集J类交流访问者的生物特征信息和其他信息,从而加强(印刷页第44988页)政府对这些外国人的监督和监控。
As with F nonimmigrants, DHS believes that replacing admissions for D/S for J-1s with admission for a fixed time period will help mitigate the national security concerns described above. Exchange visitor program categories include college and university students, which share similarities with the F-1 nonimmigrant classification. Students enrolled in such programs are pursuing post-secondary studies alongside F-1 nonimmigrants. J-1 college and university students in a degree program may be authorized to participate in the exchange visitor program so long as they meet the requirements for duration of participation, including pursuing a full course of study, echoing the full course of study requirements for F-1 nonimmigrants. A J-1 exchange visitor's program may also be extended by the ROs, subject to regulation and/or approval by DoS, without an application to DHS. These similarities give rise to the same concerns about national security related to F-1s, as described above, and about fraud and abuse by J-1s and their ROs. By requiring the same fixed period of admission for F-1s and J-1s, J-1 college and university students in exchange visitor programs will be unable to circumvent the intent of this rule,[98] which is to protect the integrity of these programs and provide additional protections and mechanisms for oversight. Because J exchange visitors are also tracked in SEVIS, DHS believes it will be more effective for an immigration officer to periodically confirm that an alien has properly maintained status, rather than relying on the checks of an RO that the J-1 is pursuing the activities permitted by the exchange visitor program. As noted above, DHS believes it is more appropriate for immigration officers, with their background checks, clearances, and training from the U.S. government, to adjudicate maintenance of nonimmigrant status and whether an alien is eligible for an additional admission period. Switching from D/S to a fixed period of admission will permit immigration officers the opportunity to determine whether an alien is eligible for an additional period of time. If an officer finds a violation of status while adjudicating the alien's request, the consequences could be immediate. Applicants for EOS must also establish that they are admissible, and failure to do so will result in denial of the EOS.[99] Admissibility grounds are complex and are properly assessed by a trained DHS officer. Such an assessment is not currently made when J exchange visitors apply for an extension of their program with their RO.[100] Thus, admitting J exchange visitors for a fixed period, instead of for D/S, will give DHS more frequent opportunities to directly vet these foreign visitors and ensure they are bona fide exchange visitors, and it will prevent and deter nefarious actors within the J exchange visitor population. Under the changes to the period of admission of J exchange visitors and the applicable EOS process, DHS may more frequently collect biometrics and other information from J exchange visitors, enhancing the ( printed page 44988) Government's oversight and monitoring of these aliens.
4. I类签证类别中存在的风险
4. Risks Within the I Classification
对大多数I类非移民签证持有人按“在美逗留期限”许可入境,使其享受与大多数其他非移民不同的待遇,后者通常按指定期限获准入境。国土安全部认为,以固定期限临时准许外国人入境美国,将加强审查和信息收集工作,并有助于移民官员确保I类非移民正在从事且将继续从事《移民与国籍法》第101(a)(15)(I)条所允许的活动。此外,本规则要求希望在其获准停留期限届满后继续保持I类非移民身份的个人向美国公民及移民服务局(USCIS)申请延期居留,届时移民官员可以审查其在美国的活动情况。该规则还明确了国土安全部将要求这些个人提交何种证据以支持其延期居留申请。[101]
Admitting most I nonimmigrants for D/S affords them different treatment from most other nonimmigrants, who are admitted for a specified period of time. DHS believes admitting aliens temporarily to the United States for a fixed period will strengthen vetting and information collection and help immigration officers ensure that the I nonimmigrants are, and will be, engaged in activities that are permissible under INA 101(a)(15)(I). In addition, this rulemaking requires individuals who wish to remain in I nonimmigrant status beyond the end date of their authorized stay to apply for an EOS with USCIS, at which point immigration officers can review their activities in the United States. It also clarifies what DHS will require these individuals to present as evidence supporting their EOS request.[101]
四、对拟议规则的公众意见回应
IV. Response to Public Comments on the Proposed Rule
A. 对拟议规则的支持意见
A. Support for the Proposed Rule
1. 总体赞同
1. General Endorsement
