If the program of study or exchange program is shorter than 4 years, the nonimmigrant will be ( printed page 44997) admitted for less than 4 years, i.e., up to the program length. If the program is longer than 4 years, the rule requires nonimmigrants to apply for EOS, which is subject to USCIS adjudication. Those who wish to stay in the United States longer without leaving the country can apply to USCIS for EOS, which will provide DHS with additional mechanisms to exercise the oversight necessary to enforce our nation's immigration laws, protect the integrity of these nonimmigrant programs, and promptly detect national security concerns. This may include conducting background checks and collecting biometrics and other information from the nonimmigrants. As explained in the proposed rule, DHS believes that replacing admission for D/S for F-1 students with admission for a fixed time period will help mitigate fraud, overstays, and national security risks by ensuring an immigration official directly and periodically vets applicants for extensions of stay and, in so doing, confirms they are engaged only in activities consistent with their student status.
值得注意的是,本规则并未改变学生及交流访问者项目(SEVP)认证学校对外国学生实施额外监管的现行要求。SEVP认证学校仍须履行有关学生注册、出勤、转学、完成项目等方面的报告义务,并必须在变更发生后21日内在SEVIS系统中更新此类信息。参见8 CFR 214.3。如果一名学生获准入境4年以完成某一学习项目,但未能入学就读,SEVP认证学校将被要求在SEVIS系统中报告此信息。该学生将被视为未能维持身份,并将面临可予递解出境的事由。
Notably, this rule does not change the SEVP certified schools' existing requirements that provide additional oversight of the foreign students. SEVP certified schools continue to have reporting requirements regarding the students' enrollment, attendance, transfer, completion of the program, etc., and must make such updates in SEVIS within 21 days of the change. See8 CFR 214.3. If a student is admitted for 4 years to complete a program of study but fails to attend school, the SEVP certified school will be required to report this information in SEVIS. The student will be considered to have failed to maintain status and will be subject to grounds of removability.
然而,国土安全部认为,现有的监测和审查工作并非加强F、J和I非移民类别的唯一机制或唯一方法。事实上,其他机构和部门以及国土安全部内部各机构开展的筛查和审查工作,应当是一项协作性工作,以进一步加强国家安全和美国移民体系的完整性。此外,出于本规则中所述的原因,国土安全部认为,固定的准许停留期限和延长居留期限(EOS)要求将专门增强F、J和I非移民类别的完整性。
However, DHS believes that the existing monitoring and vetting efforts are not exclusive mechanisms nor the only approach for strengthening the F, J, and I nonimmigrant classifications. In fact, the screening and vetting efforts undertaken by other agencies and departments, as well as agencies within DHS, should be a collaborative effort that further strengthens national security and the integrity of the U.S. immigration system. Moreover, for the reasons explained in the rule, DHS believes that a fixed admission period and EOS requirements will specifically enhance the integrity of the F, J, and I nonimmigrant classification.
c. 国土安全部逾期停留数据
c. DHS Overstay Data
意见:评论者还对国土安全部提供的数据表示担忧,并质疑这些数据是否准确反映了国土安全部希望通过拟议规则加以解决的问题。一些评论者认为,国土安全部提出的逾期停留数据不完整或不准确,不足以支持本规则中的变更。多位评论者表示,鉴于逾期停留人数较低,拟议规则缺乏证据支持或理由。同样,评论者指出,该规则是对相对较少数量逾期停留案例的不成比例的过度纠正,并补充说,这一少数数字不足以证明对学术机构以及数百万守规学生实施全面变更的合理性。一位评论者指出,外国学生总体上是一个高度守规的群体,国土安全部的数据显示,2023财年F、M和J签证持有人的逾期停留率为3.67%。
Comments: Commenters also expressed concern with the data DHS provided and questioned whether it accurately captured the issues that DHS wants to rectify with the proposed rule. Some commenters contended that the overstay data put forward by DHS was incomplete or inaccurate to support the changes in the rule. Multiple commenters said that given the low number of overstays, the proposed rule lacks evidentiary support or justification. Along those lines, commenters stated that the rule was a disproportionate overcorrection to a relatively small number of overstays, adding that this small number did not justify a wholesale change that would affect academic institutions, along with millions of compliant students. A commenter noted that foreign students, overall, are a highly compliant population, with DHS data showing the overstay rate for F, M, and J visa holders to be 3.67 percent for FY 2023.
具体而言,评论者指出,拟议规则中提到的2,100例逾期停留案例,相对于美国外国学生总人数而言相对较少,他们援引各种来源称该总人数超过300万。同样,另一位评论者指出,“永久学生”问题的规模小于国土安全部所述,因为在1,582,808份活跃的SEVIS记录中,仅有2,100人被列为在2000年至2010年间以F-1学生身份入境后仍处于活跃F-1身份。[121]另一位评论者表示,所引用的2,100例外国人持F-1签证停留超过10年的案例,占2023年获准入境的160万F签证持有人的0.1%,或占1980年获准入境的26万人的0.8%,但未提供任何来源或引用依据。另一位评论者指出,过去十年的统计数据显示逾期停留率为2%至4%,具体取决于国家和外部因素,并且根据美国公认会计准则(GAAP),5%在统计上并不具有重大意义。[122]一位评论者指出,目前的数据显示,F-1签证持有人的逾期停留率仅为1.5%,远低于B-1/B-2签证6.6%的逾期停留率。一位评论者援引“门户开放”(Open Doors)数据称,超过81%的在美外国学生来自学生来源排名前20位的国家,而这些国家中大多数的逾期停留率都非常低。[123]一些评论者援引美国海关与边境保护局(CBP)2024财年《入境/出境逾期停留报告》,指出F、M和J签证持有人2.45%的逾期停留率表明该系统行之有效,这意味着97.55%的国际学生保持合法身份并遵守签证要求。[124]
Specifically, commenters noted that the 2,100 overstays referenced in the proposed rule are relatively small in comparison to the total population of foreign students in the United States, which they stated as over 3 million, citing various sources. Along those lines, another commenter noted that the issue of “the perpetual student” was smaller than what was stated by DHS, as only 2,100 individuals of the 1,582,808 active SEVIS records were listed as still being in an active F-1 status after entering as an F-1 student between 2000 and 2010.[121] Another commenter stated the cited 2,100 cases of aliens remaining on F-1 visas for over 10 years is 0.1 percent of the 1.6 million F visa holders admitted in 2023, or 0.8 percent of the 260,000 admitted in 1980 but did not provide any sources or citations. Another commenter noted the statistics for the past decade reflect a 2-4 percent overstay rate, depending on the country and outside factors, and that 5 percent is not statistically material according to Generally Accepted Accounting Principles in the U.S. (GAAP).[122] One commenter noted that current data shows F-1 visa holders have a low 1.5 percent overstay rate compared to a 6.6 percent overstay rate for B-1/B-2 visas. A commenter referenced Open Doors data, saying over 81 percent of foreign students in the U.S. come from the top 20 countries of origin for students, and most of these countries have very low overstay rates.[123] Some commenters referenced CBP's Entry/Exit Overstay Report from fiscal year 2024, stating the 2.45 percent overstay rate for F, M, and J visa holders demonstrates the system's effectiveness and means 97.55 percent of international students maintain legal status and comply with visa requirements.[124]
许多评论者指出了国土安全部逾期停留数据存在的各种问题。一位评论者提到了美国国家政策基金会(National Foundation for American Policy,简称NFAP)进行的一项法证分析,该分析得出结论认为国土安全部的方法存在缺陷。[125]该评论者表示,国土安全部所称的“逾期停留率”并非衡量非法滞留情况的指标,而是一个“上限估计值”,未能考虑到未被记录的及时离境情况以及合法的身份变更情况。该评论者进一步表示,NFAP的分析显示,随着政府自身数据的核对调整,学生和交流访问者的“疑似”逾期停留率一度下降了多达42%。该评论者总结认为,基于如此不可靠且被夸大的统计数据而推行一项大范围的惩罚性政策,是不负责任的做法。
Many commenters pointed to various issues regarding DHS overstay data. A commenter pointed to a forensic analysis by the National Foundation for American Policy (NFAP) which had concluded that DHS methodology is flawed.[125] The commenter stated that the DHS `overstay rate' is not a measure of illegal presence but an `upper-bound estimate' that fails to account for timely departures that were not recorded and lawful changes of status. The commenter further stated that the NFAP analysis shows the `suspected' overstay rate for students and exchange visitors dropping by as much as 42 percent over time as the government's own data is reconciled. The commenter concluded that a sweeping, punitive policy on such unreliable and inflated statistics is irresponsible.
同样,评论者补充说,国土安全部(DHS)关于逾期停留率的报告存在夸大之处。评论者还指出,近年来所有学生和交流访问者签证类别的总体逾期停留率均有所下降。评论者表示,国土安全部虽然援引了项目诚信方面的担忧,但未提供证据证明现行的在美停留期限(D/S)框架普遍无效,在缺乏明确数据显示存在系统性滥用的情况下,实施如此全面的结构性变革似乎为时过早。评论者指出,国土安全部未提供证据表明逾期停留的数字所反映的是在美非法居留的个人。评论者表示,国土安全部未考虑学生可能长期维持F-1身份的正当理由,例如攻读多个学位或资格证书、参加选择性实习培训(OPT),或因研究相关延误所致。其他评论者指出,学生在美国的学业生涯(印刷页码44998)若从高中延续到博士项目,将被列入2,100人名单中,并被视为潜在的滥用案例,尽管其始终遵守相关法律及政策宗旨。一位评论者建议,需要进行更多的数据分析,以确定长期维持F-1签证身份的非移民是否应被视为不合规或不被允许。
Similarly, commenters added that DHS reports of overstay rates are inflated. Commenters also noted that overall overstay rates, in all student and exchange visitor visa categories, have fallen in recent years. Commenters stated DHS cites program integrity concerns but does not provide evidence that the existing D/S framework is broadly ineffective and without clear data showing systemic abuse, imposing such sweeping structural changes seems premature. Commenters remarked that DHS did not provide evidence that the overstay numbers reflected individuals who are unlawfully present in the United States. Commenters stated that DHS did not consider legitimate reasons why students might remain in F-1 status for extended periods, such as pursuing multiple academic degrees or certifications, participating in OPT, or a result of research-related delays. Other commenters noted that students whose academic career in the United States ( printed page 44998) had spanned from high school to a doctoral program would be included in the list of 2,100 and viewed as a potential abuse case, despite remaining compliant within the laws and intent of the policy. A commenter suggested that additional data analysis would be necessary to determine if nonimmigrants maintaining an F-1 visa status for an extended duration should be regarded as non-compliant or impermissible.
评论者表示,国土安全部的《入境/出境逾期停留报告》存在重大方法论问题,夸大了逾期停留的数字。评论者进一步指出,这些报告将已合法变更身份、调整为永久居民身份,或已离开美国但其离境未被正确记录的个人计入“逾期停留”人数之中。评论者援引国土安全部2023财年《入境/出境逾期停留报告》,显示F、M和J签证持有人在境内的逾期停留率约为3%。[126]这意味着超过97%的学生和交流访问者遵守了移民规定。同样,一位评论者援引国土安全部2020年的一份报告,显示所有F、M和J类非移民中有1.21%的人超过签证期限停留;该评论者据此认为,现行制度是有效的,拟议规则并无必要。[127]一位评论者表示,F、J和M签证持有人在2023财年疑似境内逾期停留者中仅占约9.7%,超过90%的疑似逾期停留者来自其他非移民类别,主要是短期访问签证。[128]
Commenters stated that DHS's Entry/Exit Overstay Reports contained significant methodological issues that inflated overstay numbers. Commenters further stated that these reports counted as individuals who had lawfully changed status, adjusted to permanent residency, or departed the United States but whose exits were not properly recorded as “overstays.” Commenters cited DHS's FY 2023 Entry/Exit Overstay Report showing that the in-country overstay rate for F, M, and J visa holders was around 3 percent.[126] Meaning that over 97 percent of students and exchange visitors complied with immigration requirements. Similarly, a commenter cited a 2020 DHS report indicating that 1.21 percent of all F, M, and J nonimmigrants overstayed their visa duration; the commenter reasoned that the current system is therefore effective, and the proposed rule is unwarranted.[127] One commenter stated that F, J, and M visa holders represented only about 9.7 percent of all suspected in-country overstays for FY 2023, with over 90 percent of suspected overstays coming from other nonimmigrant categories, primarily short-term visitor visas.[128]
此外,一位评论者表示,国土安全部的数据系统在核对离境信息方面经常存在滞后,导致逾期停留率被高报,直到这些系统更新以显示准确的逾期停留率为止。评论者援引人口统计学家罗伯特·沃伦(Robert Warren)与国家外国政策基金会(NFAP)的研究,指出超过一半被报告为“逾期停留”的人实际上已经离境。[129]然而,这些离境情况并未被记录在案。另一位评论者对国土安全部的逾期停留数据表示担忧,原因是该系统存在错误和漏洞。该评论者指出,美国海关与边境保护局(CBP)在学生及交流访问者信息系统(SEVIS)中多次未能准确记录入境或离境日期,且该数据并未设有具体的数据类别,以统计有多少人在几天、一周或一个月内离开美国。
Additionally, a commenter stated that DHS's data systems frequently lag in reconciling departures, resulting in overstay rates being overreported, until these systems update to show the accurate overstay rate. Commenters cited research, by demographer Robert Warren and the NFAP, stating that more than half of reported “overstays” had actually departed the country.[129] However, these departures were not recorded as such. Another commenter expressed concern with overstay data from DHS due to errors and gaps in the system. The commenter pointed out multiple instances where arrival or departure dates were not captured accurately by CBP in SEVIS, and the data did not have specific data categories for how many individuals departed the United States within a few days, a week, or a month.
一条评论批评国土安全部未提供有关J-1交流访问者的数据,并表示拟议规则本应排除教授和研究学者类别,因为该类别的项目期限最长为五年;短期学者类别的项目期限最长为六个月;专家类别的项目期限最长为一年。
A comment criticized that DHS did not provide data on J-1 Exchange Visitors and stated that the proposed rule should have excluded professor and research scholar categories, who are limited to program duration of five years maximum; short-term scholars limited to program duration of six months maximum; and specialists limited to program duration of one year maximum.
回应:国土安全部不认同这些评论的总体前提。本规则的目的和必要性并不仅仅取决于逾期停留人数本身。国土安全部提供的逾期停留统计数据,结合欺诈案例、国家安全问题,以及非移民学生在美国长期滞留的情况,从整体角度看,共同凸显了制定本规则的必要性。正如《拟议规则制定通知》(NPRM)中所强调的,这些问题表明了在美停留期限(D/S)框架所存在的欺诈、国家安全及其他相关问题。本规则提供了令人信服的案例,表明在D/S框架下存在欺诈、滥用及国家安全方面的担忧,以及非移民学生在美国长期滞留的情况,这些均对美国的利益构成严重威胁。
Response: DHS disagrees with the general premise of these comments. The purpose and need for the rule does not merely hinge on the number of overstays alone. DHS provided overstay statistics, coupled with cases of fraud, national security concerns, and nonimmigrant students remaining in the United States for lengthy periods of time, which viewed wholistically, underscore the need for this rule. Such concerns, as highlighted in the NPRM, demonstrate the fraud, national security, and other issues associated with the D/S framework. The rule provides compelling cases of fraud, abuse, and national security concerns, and nonimmigrant students remaining in the United States for lengthy periods of time under the D/S framework, which pose serious threats to the interests of the United States.
在拟议规则的序言中,美国国土安全部(DHS)指出,以D/S身份获准入境并不能为移民官员提供足够的预定机会,以直接核实获得此类非移民身份的外国人在美国境内仅从事其各自身份所允许的活动。这削弱了国土安全部有效执行与非法居留相关的法定不可入境理由的能力,并造成了国家安全漏洞以及欺诈和滥用的诱因。
In the preamble to the proposed rule, DHS pointed out that admission for D/S does not afford immigration officers enough predetermined opportunities to directly verify that aliens granted such nonimmigrant statuses are engaging only in those activities their respective classifications authorize while they are in the United States. This has undermined DHS's ability to effectively enforce compliance with statutory inadmissibility grounds related to unlawful presence and has created national security vulnerabilities and incentives for fraud and abuse.
国土安全部认为,本规则将提供机制来解决围绕F、J和I项目完整性的部分问题。该规则对于加强F、J和I类非移民身份管理中的监督和问责制是必要的。虽然F-1身份延长期限的情形看似微不足道或出于合法目的,但此类情形中存在滥用或欺诈的可能性,凸显了实施确保遵守移民法措施的重要性。国土安全部认识到,F-1身份期限延长可能是出于合理的学术或专业原因,并无意因学生遵守其身份条款的合法活动而对其进行处罚。该规则旨在解决当前系统中的漏洞,并最终加强F、J和I类非移民项目的完整性,同时承认学生可能正在从事合法的学术和专业活动。国土安全部已仔细考虑了该规则的潜在影响,并认为其带来的益处,包括改善监督以及侦测和防止欺诈的能力,证明实施该规则是合理的。有关该规则总体经济影响分析的全面讨论,请参见第VI.A、B和C节。
DHS believes that this rule will provide the mechanisms to address some of the concerns surrounding the integrity of F, J, and I programs. The rule is necessary to enhance oversight and accountability in the administration of F, J, and I nonimmigrant statuses. While cases of extended F-1 duration may seemingly appear to be insignificant or for legitimate purposes, the potential for misuse or fraud in such cases underscores the importance of implementing measures to ensure compliance with immigration laws. DHS recognizes that extended F-1 durations may occur for valid academic or professional reasons and does not intend to penalize students for lawful activities that comply with the terms of their status. The rule is designed to address vulnerabilities in the current system and ultimately to strengthen the integrity of the F, J, and I nonimmigrant programs while recognizing that students may be engaged in legitimate academic and professional pursuits. DHS has carefully considered the potential impacts of the rule and believes that its benefits, including improved oversight and the ability to detect and prevent fraud, justify its implementation. See secs. VI.A, B, and C for a full discussion of the rule's overall economic impact analysis.
关于数据不准确或不完整的问题,国土安全部指出,尽管移民官员在向学生及交流访问者信息系统(SEVIS)及其他系统录入数据时可能存在人为错误,但国土安全部认为个别情况不会对国土安全部记录的可靠性或本规则的目的造成重大影响。
With respect to inaccurate or incomplete data, DHS notes that while there may be human error involved in data entry into SEVIS and elsewhere by immigration officers, DHS does not believe that isolated instances greatly impact the reliability of DHS records nor the purpose of this rule.
同样,国土安全部不同意J-1非移民逾期居留率并不显著的观点。根据学生及交流访问者项目(SEVP)《2024年SEVIS数据统计报告》,2024年约有301,000名J-1非移民入境美国。[130]因此,2024年J-1非移民群体中估计的逾期居留人数约为10,000人。[131]
Likewise, DHS disagrees that the overstay rate is not significant for J-1 nonimmigrants. According to SEVP's 2024 SEVIS by the Numbers Report, approximately 301,000 J-1 nonimmigrants entered the United States in 2024.[130] Therefore, the estimated overstay number from the 2024 J-1 nonimmigrant cohort would be approximately 10,000.[131]
关于国土安全部逾期居留数据使用了有缺陷的方法这一说法,国土安全部自2015财年起每个财年均发布逾期居留报告。就该报告而言,国土安全部将非移民视为逾期居留的情形包括:截至数据提取日期,(1)存在记录显示其在获准停留期限结束后才离境的(即“境外逾期居留”),或(2)在获准停留期限结束前,没有离境、延期、身份变更或身份调整的记录(即“疑似境内逾期居留”)。逾期居留率是指报告所涵盖的入境人数中符合上述标准的人数所占的比例。
As far as DHS overstay data using a flawed methodology, DHS has released overstay reports each fiscal year since 2015. For the purpose of the report, DHS counts a nonimmigrant as an overstay if, as of the data pull date, (1) a record exists of a departure that occurred after the end of the authorized period of ( printed page 44999) admission ( i.e., an “out of country overstay”), or (2) no record of a departure, extension, change of status, or adjustment of status before the end of the authorized period of admission ( i.e., a “suspected in-country overstay”). The overstay rate is the share of admissions covered by the report that meet these criteria.
国土安全部利用美国海关与边境保护局(CBP)的入境与离境信息系统(ADIS)编制这些数据,该系统整合了承运人的入境和离境舱单、部分伙伴国家的陆路离境数据,以及美国公民及移民服务局(USCIS)提供的移民福利和身份信息,包括延期、身份变更和身份调整信息。国土安全部通过与这些数据来源进行交叉核对,来缩小疑似逾期居留人员的名单范围。
DHS produces these figures using CBP's Arrival and Departure Information System (ADIS), which consolidates carrier arrival and departure manifests, certain partner country land exit data, and immigration benefit and status information from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), including extensions, changes of status, and adjustments. DHS narrows the list of suspected overstays by cross-checking against these data sources.
正如美国国家外国人政策基金会(NFAP)所指出的,疑似境内逾期居留人数随时间推移而下降,这反映了国土安全部在收到更多离境和福利信息后更新记录这一预期且有据可查的过程。这种下降是系统设计所预期的结果,而非方法上的缺陷。这些后续调整的存在是该方法众所周知且透明的特征,并不意味着初始统计数据不可靠或存在“夸大”情况。
The decline over time in counts of suspected in-country overstays, as noted by NFAP, reflects the expected and documented process of updating records as DHS receives additional departure and benefit information. This decline is an intended result of the system design, not a flaw in the methodology. The existence of these later adjustments is a known and transparent feature of the methodology and does not mean the initial statistics are unreliable or “inflated.”
与所有行政数据集一样,ADIS系统存在少量数据错误、报告不完整、记录匹配不完善及相关数据质量问题,但国土安全部在十多年来一直稳步致力于识别和消除这些错误。虽然任何给定的ADIS个人记录可能仍存在数据质量问题,但所报告的总体逾期滞留率总体上是可靠的,适用于对不同国家、准许入境类别以及不同时期进行比较。
Like all administrative datasets, the ADIS system is subject to a small number of data errors, incomplete reporting, imperfect record matching, and related data quality problems, but the Department has worked steadily to identify and eliminate these errors over more than a decade. While any given individual ADIS record may be subject to remaining data quality problems, reported aggregate overstay rates are generally reliable and suitable for making comparisons across countries and classes of admission and over time.
国土安全部(DHS)还指出,在“在美停留期限”(D/S)框架下追踪逾期滞留数据是困难的,且容易出现统计不足的情况。若以固定期限准许入境,逾期滞留数据将更易于追踪和评估。此外,逾期滞留现象加之“在美停留期限”框架所固有的脆弱性,包括对国家安全构成的更高风险,引发了严重关切。如序言中所述,本规则为国土安全部提供了一种机制,使其能够定期、直接地评估这些非移民是否遵守其身份类别的条件及美国移民法律。以固定期限准许入境将减少逾期滞留现象,因为违规者将在其获准入境期限届满后开始累积非法居留时间,并可能根据《移民与国籍法》第212(a)(9)(B)和(C)条(即8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(9)(B)和(C)条)的规定,在离开美国时因该非法居留累积而被认定为不可准许入境。
DHS also notes tracking overstay data under the D/S framework is difficult and prone to undercounting. Tracking overstay data will be easier to track and assess with admission for a fixed period. Furthermore, overstays coupled with the vulnerabilities of the D/S framework, including heightened risks to national security, pose serious concerns. As explained in the preamble, this rule provides a mechanism for DHS to periodically and directly assess whether these nonimmigrants are complying with the conditions of their classifications and U.S. immigration laws. Admission for a fixed period of time will reduce overstays, as violators will begin to accrue unlawful presence following the expiration of their authorized period of admission and may become inadmissible based on that accrual of unlawful presence under INA section 212(a)(9)(B) and (C), 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(9)(B) and (C), upon departing the United States.
4. 对美国政府的负面影响
4. Negative Impacts to the U.S. Government
a. 现行制度的充分性与行政负担
a. Sufficiency of Current System and Administrative Burdens
评论意见:有评论者指出,学生与交流访问者信息系统(SEVIS)的报告与追踪制度、实地访查以及现行的裁决程序已经足够,拟议规则并不会提供更大程度的监督。具体而言,评论者指出,现行SEVIS系统已经为国土安全部提供了充分的监督,对学术选择施加僵化的联邦限制属于过度干预,弊大于利。部分评论者表示,该规则造成法律上的混乱及执法问题,取消“在美停留期限”标注并引入固定截止日期,与SEVIS及大学合规办公室目前的运作方式相冲突。另一位评论者指出,“在美停留期限”政策多年来一直支持着一代又一代的外国学生和学者,同时维护了项目的完整性,促进了教育流动性,并通过SEVIS监督维护了国家安全,该评论者认为拟议的变更将损害学生利益,加重大学资源负担,削弱美国高等教育的全球地位,而几乎没有证据表明有必要进行此类改革。
Comments: Commenters stated the SEVIS reporting and tracking system, site visits, and current adjudications are sufficient and that the proposed rule would not provide any greater oversight. Specifically, commenters pointed out that the current SEVIS system already provides DHS with significant oversight and that imposing rigid federal restrictions on academic choices is an overreach that will cause more harm than good. Some commenters stated that the rule creates legal confusion and enforcement problems and that eliminating the D/S notation and introducing fixed end dates conflict with how SEVIS and university compliance offices currently function. Another commenter pointed out that the D/S policy has supported generations of foreign students and scholars while preserving program integrity, facilitating educational mobility, and maintaining national security through SEVIS oversight, and asserted that the proposed change would harm students, strain university resources, and weaken the global standing of U.S. higher education—with little evidence of the need for such reform.
多位评论者担忧,拟议规则只会与SEVIS及国务院目前所做的工作重复,且由于这些新变更带来的巨大行政负担,美国公民及移民服务局(USCIS)将不堪重负。另一位评论者指出,目前的SEVIS流程更加及时、准确,因为USCIS目前的处理时间约为3.5个月,而SEVIS要求指定学校官员(DSO)或负责官员(ARO)在21个日历日内报告,学生或学者则需在10个日历日内报告。一位评论者表示,USCIS的裁决人员将难以复制目前在DSO、ARO与学生与交流访问者项目(SEVP)外勤代表之间已经形成的、对各高校及校园个别制度的理解。部分评论者写道,决定学生学业路径的权力应继续由学术机构掌握,而DSO是训练有素的专业人员,最有资格核实学生的学业状况和意图。
Several commenters expressed concern that the proposed rule would only duplicate efforts currently undertaken by SEVIS and the State Department, and USCIS would be overwhelmed due to the substantial administrative burden from these new changes. Another commented that the current SEVIS process is timelier and more accurate as the current processing time for USCIS is around 3.5 months, but SEVIS requires reporting within 21 calendar days for a DSO or an ARO and 10 calendar days for a student or scholar. One commenter stated that it would be hard for USCIS adjudicators to replicate the understanding of individual systems at colleges and campuses that has already formed between DSOs, AROs, and SEVP field representatives under the current process. Some commenters wrote that the authority to determine a student's academic path should remain with the academic institutions and that DSOs are trained professionals who are best positioned to verify a student's academic standing and intentions.
此外,评论者指出,拟议规则采取“一刀切”的做法,将执法资源浪费在低风险群体身上,而非用于应对真正的威胁。由于该群体已经在SEVIS下接受过审查,一位评论者写道,拟议规则下的变更将使国土安全部的资源从调查高优先级威胁(如国家支持的间谍活动、网络战和恐怖主义)中转移出去。
Additionally, commenters stated that the proposed rule's blanket approach wastes enforcement resources on low-risk populations rather than actual threats. Due to this population already being vetted under SEVIS, one commenter wrote that the changes under the proposed rule would divert DHS resources away from investigating high-priority threats, such as state-sponsored espionage, cyber warfare, and terrorism.
回应:国土安全部(DHS)承认,现有机制,例如学生和交流访问者信息系统(SEVIS),总体上为外国学生、外国交流访问者和教育机构提供了监督。然而,国土安全部认为,现有的监测和审查工作并非强化F类、J类和I类非移民身份的唯一机制或唯一方法。此外,国土安全部不同意仅依靠SEVIS中的数据来识别学生或交流访问者身份可能存在的违规行为,就足以解决“维持身份期限”(D/S)框架存在的脆弱性问题这一观点。
Response: DHS acknowledges that existing mechanisms, such as SEVIS, provide oversight of foreign students, foreign exchange visitors, and educational institutions in general. However, DHS believes that the existing monitoring and vetting efforts are not exclusive mechanisms nor the only approach for strengthening the F, J, and I nonimmigrant classifications. Moreover, DHS disagrees that leveraging data in SEVIS alone to identify possible student or exchange visitor status violations is sufficient to address the vulnerabilities of the D/S framework.
SEVIS在一定程度上依赖于教育机构和项目担保方录入的信息。尽管国土安全部认可指定学校官员(DSO)和负责官员(RO)通常与非移民学生和交流访问者有频繁互动,但国土安全部认为,适当的做法是由DSO遵守其所在学校或项目担保方以及F类和J类非移民人群的SEVIS报告要求,而由国土安全部作出移民身份方面的认定,例如延长移民身份以及评估外国人是否仍符合该非移民类别的资格条件。DSO和RO不能履行移民官员的职责。例如,DSO可能并不知晓某学生未能维持身份的情形,包括因从事犯罪活动而导致的身份丧失。他们可以建议延长项目期限,但只有移民官员才能裁决延长身份(EOS)申请,并就身份和可入境性作出法律认定。DSO和RO不应再充当移民官员的直接代理人,尽管他们将继续履行重要职责,协助国土安全部以及非移民学生和交流访问者。
In part, SEVIS relies on information that is inputted by educational institutions and program sponsors. While DHS appreciates that DSOs and ROs generally interact frequently with nonimmigrant students and exchange visitors, DHS believes it is appropriate for DSOs to comply with SEVIS reporting requirements for their school or program sponsors and F and J nonimmigrant population, but for DHS to make immigration status determinations, such as extending an immigration status and assessing whether an alien remains eligible for the nonimmigrant classification. DSOs and ROs cannot perform the duties of immigration officers. For example, DSOs may be unaware of a student's failure to maintain status, including by engaging in criminal activity. They may recommend program extensions, but only immigration officers can adjudicate EOS applications and make legal determinations about status and admissibility. DSOs and ROs should no longer serve as direct proxies for immigration officers, though they will continue to perform important duties to assist DHS and nonimmigrant students and exchange visitors.
在“维持身份期限”(D/S)框架下,除非F类、J类或I类非移民申请变更为其他非移民身份,或向美国公民及移民服务局(USCIS)申请其他福利,否则在该外国人身处美国期间,不要求进行背景调查。这造成了这样一种情况:F类、J类和I类非移民可能在美国长期停留,而未经过以延长身份(EOS)申请形式(包括随附的背景调查)或后续签证申请或在入境口岸(POE)接受检查形式进行的美国政府审查。(印刷页第45000页)规定固定期限的入境许可将减少逾期停留的情形,因为违规者将在其获准停留期限届满后开始累积非法居留,并可能根据《移民与国籍法》(INA)第212(a)(9)(B)条和第(C)条,即《美国法典》第8编第1182(a)(9)(B)条和第(C)条的规定,在其离开美国时因该非法居留累积而被认定为不可入境。尽管一些评论者呼吁采取更具针对性的审查方法,但国土安全部坚称,固定入境期限和延长身份申请要求并非惩罚性规定,也并非专门针对F类、J类和I类非移民。值得注意的是,该新规使其他非移民类别的法规和程序更加趋于一致。
Under the D/S framework, there are no background checks required while the alien is in the United States unless the F, J, or I nonimmigrant applies for a change of status to a different nonimmigrant status, or another benefit with USCIS. This has created situations where F, J, and I nonimmigrants can be present for long periods in the United States without undergoing U.S. government review in the form of an ( printed page 45000) EOS application, including accompanying background checks, or subsequent visa application or inspection at a POE. Admission for a fixed period of time will reduce overstays, as violators will begin to accrue unlawful presence following the expiration of their authorized period of admission and may become inadmissible based on that accrual of unlawful presence under INA section 212(a)(9)(B) and (C), 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(9)(B) and (C), upon departing the United States. While some commenters call for a more targeted approach to vetting, DHS asserts that the fixed admission period and the EOS application requirements are not punitive or specific to the F, J, and I nonimmigrants. Notably, the new rule closely aligns the regulations and procedures for other nonimmigrant classifications.
b. 国家安全项目与自我报告
b. National Security Programs and Self-Reporting
评论意见:有评论者提供了具体实例,说明可利用已经建立的项目来实现拟议规则所设定的目标。评论者还指出,目前已有应对国家安全威胁的相关项目。一位评论者指出,美国国务院已经对资金来源、远亲关系、旅行计划、此前赴美旅行记录、社交媒体活动、就业和教育情况,以及在美国的工作或学习计划展开调查。该评论者表示,依靠个人自行报告身份违规或犯罪行为不会强化国家安全,并且I-539延长身份申请表第4部分所列问题,与DS-160表中所载简化版问题类似。一位评论者指出,由国土安全调查局(HSI)主导的“校园哨兵”(Campus Sentinel)项目,目前仍在反威胁线索研判小组(CTLD)下保持活跃,并已对学生和校园合规情况进行监测。另一位评论者指出,美国国务院和国土安全部已经对I类签证申请人实施监督,因为此类申请人在获准入境前必须接受美国领事官员的审查。还有一位评论者建议国土安全部将目前用于移民执法的联邦调查局(FBI)探员和缉毒署(DEA)探员重新调配,转而应对国家安全威胁。
Comments: Commenters provided specific instances where already established programs could be used to achieve the goals set forth under the proposed rule. Commenters also noted that there are programs already in place to deal with national security threats. One commenter noted that the DoS already investigates funding sources, extended family, travel plans, previous travel to the United States, social media activity, employment and education, and planned work or education in the United States. The commenter stated that relying on individuals to self-report violations of status or crimes would not strengthen national security, and the questions posted in Part 4 of the I-539 extension of status application are similar to the abbreviation version found in the DS-160. A commenter noted that Project Campus Sentinel, led by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), currently remains active under the Counter Threat Lead Development Unit (CTLD) and already monitors students and campus compliance. Another commenter noted that there is already oversight by the DoS and DHS for I visa applicants as they must undergo vetting by U.S. consular officers before admission. Another commenter recommended DHS divert FBI agents and DEA agents who are currently being used for immigration enforcement back to national security threats.
答复:国土安全部(DHS)承认,目前存在其他现行机制,可加强对学生、教育机构以及外国人总体的监督。然而,国土安全部不同意评论者关于现有机制已经足够的观点。国土安全部认为,现有的监测和审查工作并非唯一的机制,也不是加强F、J和I非移民类别管理的唯一途径。事实上,其他机构和部门以及国土安全部内部各机构所开展的筛查、审查和调查工作,应作为一项协作努力,进一步加强国家安全和美国移民制度的完整性。
Response: DHS acknowledges that there are other existing mechanisms that enhance oversight of students, educational institutions, and foreign nationals in general. However, DHS disagrees with commenters that the existing mechanisms are sufficient. DHS believes that the existing monitoring and vetting efforts are not exclusive mechanisms nor the only approach for strengthening the F, J, and I nonimmigrant classifications. In fact, the screening, vetting, and investigating efforts undertaken by other agencies and departments, as well as agencies within DHS, should be a collaborative effort that further strengthens national security and the integrity of the U.S. immigration system.
此外,国土安全部认为,关于自我申报的评论是有误导性的。该规则并非主要依赖外国人的自我申报。该规则规定,作为F、J和I类非移民身份延长(EOS)申请程序的一部分,美国公民及移民服务局(USCIS)可要求按照8 CFR 103.16的规定采集生物识别信息(如指纹、照片和签名),申请人也可能被要求出席面谈。参见8 CFR 103.2(b)(9)。采集生物识别信息的目的在于确认申请人身份、进行背景和安全审查,并筛查是否存在国家安全或欺诈方面的隐患。EOS申请要求是加强政府监督和监测的一种方式,确保个人不对国家安全构成威胁,因为生物识别信息采集和背景审查将更为频繁地进行。
Furthermore, DHS asserts that the comment on self-reporting is misguided. The rule does not largely rely on self-reporting by foreign nationals. The rule provides that as part of the EOS application process for F, J, and I nonimmigrants, USCIS may require the collection of biometrics (such as fingerprints, photographs, and signatures) as may be required by 8 CFR 103.16, and applicants may be required to appear for an interview. See8 CFR 103.2(b)(9). The purpose of collecting biometrics is to confirm the individual's identity, conduct background and security checks, and screen for any national security or fraud concerns. The EOS application requirement is a way to enhance government oversight and monitoring, and to ensure that individuals do not pose a threat to national security, as biometrics and background checks will be conducted more frequently.
5. 对高等教育的影响
5. Impacts to Higher Education
a. 招生情况
a. Enrollment
评论意见:评论者表示担忧,但未提供数据支持,认为拟议规则可能导致美国院校的外国学生入学人数下降,部分人估计降幅为10%至15%,另一些人估计为20%至30%。评论者表示,这可能加剧本已下滑的入学水平。其他人指出,该规则带来的不必要、重复且浪费性的流程将影响愿意赴美国大学就读的学生人数,从而直接损害外国学生和学者服务机构的运营,因为其70%的薪资、系统和项目成本依赖学生费用支持。一位评论者未提供依据地表示,美国院校在2025年秋季已损失近三分之一的外国学生。评论者表示,这种下降归因于政治不稳定、对政府政策的敌意感知、签证审查力度加大以及签证预约名额有限。一位评论者提供了对《高等教育内参》(Inside Higher Ed)[132]初步数据的分析,显示美国公立院校和小型私立院校在2025年秋季的外国学生入学人数均出现下降。一位评论者描述了自2025年起即将出现的“人口悬崖”现象,原因是2007年后美国出生率下降,并表示外国学生对许多院校而言是防止入学人数不稳定的重要缓冲力量。
Comments: Commenters expressed concern, without providing data, about the proposed rule's potential to decrease foreign student enrollment in U.S. institutions, with some estimating a decrease of 10-15 percent and 20-30 percent. Commenters stated that this could exacerbate already declining enrollment levels. Others remarked that the rule's unnecessary, duplicative and wasteful process would impact numbers of students willing to study at U.S. universities, which would directly harm the operations of foreign student and scholar services since 70 percent of salaries, systems and programming costs are student fee based. A commenter stated, without support, that U.S. institutions have lost nearly one-third of their foreign students in Fall 2025. Commenters stated this decrease is attributed to political instability, perceived hostility from administration policies, increased visa vetting, and limited visa appointment availability. One commenter included an analysis of preliminary data from Inside Higher Ed,[132] which showed a decline in foreign student enrollment in Fall 2025 for both public and small private colleges in the United States. One commenter described an approaching “demographic cliff” starting in 2025 due to declining U.S. birth rates after 2007, suggesting that foreign students serve as a critical buffer against enrollment instability at many institutions.
许多评论者指出,该规则可能使美国教育机构相较于德国、中国、新加坡、加拿大或澳大利亚等提供更灵活签证制度的国家而言吸引力下降,从而阻碍潜在学生选择赴美。与此类似,一位评论者比较了在美国与其他国家留学的费用,并在未提供数据来源的情况下列出以下内容:加拿大,硕士学费为每年15,000至30,000加元(约合11,000至22,000美元),毕业生可在1至2年内申请永久居留权,工作许可申请程序简便;德国,公立大学学费为每年0至3,000欧元(约合0至3,300美元),毕业生可在2至3年内获得永久居留权,并立即获得全职工作授权;澳大利亚,硕士学费为每年30,000至45,000澳元(约合18,000至27,000美元),毕业生可凭临时毕业生签证(485类别)工作,在从事技术类工作2至4年后,可能具备申请永久居留权的资格。该评论者指出,相比之下,在美国,即便通过OPT和STEM OPT完成2至3年的学习和工作,国际毕业生也仅能选择申请H-1B签证,而该签证需通过抽签制度决定,且不保证能获得永久居留权。该评论者补充说,该规则所带来的额外负担和不确定性将降低美国教育的吸引力。
Many commenters point out how this rule could deter prospective students by making the United States educational institutions less attractive compared to countries like Germany, China, Singapore, Canada or Australia, which offer more flexible visa systems. Along the same lines, a commenter compared the cost of studying in the U.S. to other countries and discussed the following, without providing any citation for this data: Canada—Master's tuition is CAD 15,000-30,000 per year (~$11,000-$22,000 USD) and graduates can apply for permanent residence within 1-2 years, with straightforward work permits; Germany—Public universities charge €0-€3,000 per year (~$0-$3,300 USD) and graduates can obtain permanent residency in 2-3 years, with immediate full-time work authorization; Australia—Master's tuition ranges from AUD 30,000-45,000 per year (~$18,000-$27,000 USD) and graduates can work on a Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), and after 2-4 years of skilled employment, may become eligible for permanent residency. The commenter noted that in contrast, in the U.S. even after 2-3 years of study and work on OPT and STEM OPT, international graduates only had the option of H-1B visas, which are subject to the lottery system, with no guarantee to permanent residency. The commenter added that the additional burdens and uncertainty due to the rule would reduce the attractiveness of the U.S. education.
关于这一点,一位评论者指出,这一趋势将产生乘数效应,因为每一名受到负面影响的学生都会影响数十名潜在申请人。一位评论者写道,经济合作与发展组织(OECD)移民展望的数据(该评论者未提供来源)显示,提供路径可预测性的国家所吸引的STEM博士毕业生比实行严格续签要求的国家多73%,而另一位评论者指出,英国于2021年恢复的两年期毕业后工作(印刷页45001)签证在一年内导致外国学生申请增加了24%。
Relatedly, a commenter noted that this trend will have a multiplier effect as each negatively affected student influences dozens of prospective applicants. A commenter wrote that data from the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) Migration outlook (commenter did not provide a source) shows that countries offering pathway predictability capture 73 percent more STEM doctoral graduates than those with rigid renewal requirements, while another commenter stated that the UK's restoration of two-year post-study work ( printed page 45001) visas in 2021 resulted in a 24 percent increase in foreign student application within one year.
多位评论者指出,社区学院也将受到影响,因为社区学院可以作为通往大学的渠道,而拟议规则可能阻碍转学过程,从而使申请人不愿就读社区学院。多位评论者表示,拟议规则将使社区学院更难招收学生,并将增加其工作量。评论者指出,外国学生并不会取代本国学生,部分评论者引用了美国国家外国政策基金会(NFAP)的研究,该研究发现,公立大学每多招收一名国际本科生,平均就会多招收两名州内一年级新生。[133]
Several commenters noted that community colleges will also be impacted as they can be pipelines to universities, and the proposed rule may hinder the transfer process and thereby discourage applicants from enrolling in community colleges. Several commenters said the proposed rule would make it more difficult for community colleges to enroll students and would increase their workload. Commenters stated that foreign students do not displace domestic students, with some citing research from the NFAP which found that for every additional international undergraduate student enrolled, on average two more in-state first-year students enrolled at public universities.[133]
回应：国土安全部（DHS）承认,由于本规则,外国学生在美国教育机构的入学率可能会下降,但由于没有先例可以据此得出关于本规则影响的准确结论,因此国土安全部无法量化这一下降的程度。然而,国土安全部并不打算使本规则导致外国学生入学率大幅下降。如前所述,外国学生入学水平本身就会波动,因此断言任何下降完全是本规则的直接且唯一结果,属于推测。[134]任何下降都可能包括部分不打算遵守或此前未遵守其非移民身份条件的潜在或现有外国学生。
Response: DHS acknowledges that enrollment of foreign students in U.S. educational institutions may decline because of this rule but is unable to quantify the extent of this decline because there is no precedent from which accurate conclusions can be drawn as to the rule's impact. However, DHS does not intend for the rule to result in a significant decline in foreign student enrollment. As noted, the level of foreign student enrollment does fluctuate, and it is speculative to assess any declination is a direct and sole result of the rule.[134] Any decline would likely include some prospective or current foreign students who do not intend to comply or have not been complying with the conditions of their nonimmigrant classification.
国土安全部认识到,外国学生在稳定许多院校(包括作为通往大学渠道的社区学院)的入学率和维持其财务健康方面发挥着作用。国土安全部在起草本规则时已经考虑了评论者就区域和州一级经济影响所引用的资料,以及所有潜在影响。国土安全部最终得出结论,本规则带来的益处超过了入学率可能下降及随之而来的经济影响。
DHS recognizes foreign students play a role in stabilizing enrollment and supporting the financial health of many institutions, including community colleges that serve as pipelines to universities. DHS has considered commenters' citations regarding economic impacts regionally and at the state level and all the potential impacts when drafting this rule. DHS has ultimately concluded the benefits to the rule outweigh any potential decreases to enrollment and subsequent economic impacts.
b. 对学术项目、研究及STEM领域的影响
b. Impact on Academic Programs and Research and STEM
评论意见：许多评论者对本规则关于固定准许停留期限和境内身份延期(EOS)要求的规定可能对教育和研究项目造成的影响表示担忧。具体而言,多位评论者担心,由于本规则规定的4年固定准许停留期限,包括许多博士学位在内的、学制超过四年的项目将面临风险。评论者表示,本规则从根本上与美国高等教育的实际学术格局不符。一位评论者指出,综合高等教育数据系统衡量的是6年内完成学士学位的情况,而联邦学生资助资格认定的学业进展合格标准则是公布学制长度的150%。据评论者称,数据显示,56%的本科生需要超过4年才能完成学位项目，而双学位由于核心课程重叠且繁重,需要5到6年时间。评论者特别指出,许多STEM博士项目需要五年以上的培训时间才能确保掌握本领域知识,四年时间并不充分。一位评论者指出,根据美国国家科学基金会（NSF）的数据,工程学博士平均完成时间为6.7年,理科博士平均为6.1年,而按照拟议的4年期限,引领量子计算、人工智能、生物技术和先进材料等突破性技术的研究人员将转而前往其他国家。另一位评论者指出,根据美国物理联合会的数据,物理学博士的平均完成时间为六年,且约有16%的学生需要八年或更长时间才能完成学位。
Comments: Many commenters raised concerns regarding the impact on educational and research programs due to the rule's provisions on fixed admission period and EOS requirements. Specifically, multiple commenters raised concerns that programs lasting longer than the four years, including many doctorate degrees, are in jeopardy due to the 4-year fixed admission period provided in the rule. Commenters stated this rule is fundamentally misaligned with the actual academic landscape of U.S. higher education. A commenter noted the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System measures successful completion of a bachelor's degree within 6 years, while Federal Financial Aid eligibility identifies satisfactory academic progress standards at 150 percent of the published program length. According to commenters, for undergraduate students, data shows that 56 percent take more than 4 years to complete the degree program, and double majors require 5 to 6 years due to overlapping and intensive core curricula. Commenters particularly stated that many STEM doctoral programs require more than five years of training to ensure mastery within the field and that four years is not sufficient. One commenter noted that based on NSF data, engineering Ph.D. completion is on average 6.7 years and science Ph.D.s average 6.1 years, and with the proposed limit at 4 years, researchers who are behind breakthrough technologies, such as quantum computing, AI, biotechnology, and advanced materials, will go elsewhere. Another commenter noted that according to the American Institute of Physics, the average time to complete a Ph.D. in physics is six years and that approximately 16 percent of students take eight years or more to complete their degrees.
评论者指出，该规则将对美国大学、研究、经济及全球竞争力产生负面影响，因为外国学生通过学费、住房及创新（例如在STEM领域）为美国经济贡献了数十亿美元。另一位评论者指出，该规则每年将产生数亿美元的合规成本，其中大部分将由美国大学和研究机构承担，而这些资金本可用于资助教室、实验室或执法重点事项。鉴于申请延长身份（EOS）的时间安排以及项目可能被中断的风险，评论者指出，拟议规则可能会减缓或扰乱美国大学的研究成果，并削弱美国在科学领域的领导地位。一些评论者指出，为外国出生学生引入制度上的不确定性，从长远来看也会损害研究的连续性和创新能力。
Commenters pointed out that the rule would have a negative impact on U.S. universities, research, economy, and global competitiveness, as foreign students contribute billions to the U.S. economy through tuition, housing, and innovation ( e.g., in STEM fields). Another commenter stated the rule would impose hundreds of millions of dollars in annual compliance costs, much of which would fall on U.S. universities and research institutions, which could otherwise fund classrooms, laboratories, or enforcement priorities. Given the timelines for requesting EOS and the potential for projects to be interrupted, commenters noted that the proposed rule could slow down or disrupt research outcomes at U.S. universities and weaken U.S. leadership in the field of science. Some commenters noted that the introduction of uncertainty in the system for foreign born students would also harm research continuity and innovation in the long run.
最后，一位评论者指出，美国接收了经济合作与发展组织（OECD）成员国中大部分的国际博士生，使赴美留学变得更加不可预测，将损害美国的国家安全和经济竞争力。
Lastly, a commenter noted that the United States hosts many of the world's international doctoral students across Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) countries, and making studying in the United States less predictable would undermine the United States national security and economic competitiveness.
回应：国土安全部（DHS）认识到，该规则将要求利益相关方，特别是学生、研究人员和教育机构实施变革。然而，国土安全部认为，这些负担被该规则带来的益处所抵消，该规则为国土安全部建立了一种机制，以加强审查、减少逾期居留，并确定非移民是否遵守其非移民身份的相关条件。本最终规则所施加的要求使美国政府有更多机会审查非移民的记录、入境资格以及任何可能表明欺诈、滥用或国家安全问题的迹象。该规则旨在通过为移民官员提供预先确定的时间点，直接评估F、J和I类非移民是否维持其身份，来解决“在校学习期限”（D/S）框架所带来的漏洞问题，正如国土安全部对其他非移民类别所采取的做法一样。
Response: DHS recognizes that the rule will require implementing changes by the stakeholders, especially students, researchers, and educational institutions. However, DHS believes that such burdens are outweighed by the benefits of this rule, which creates a mechanism for DHS to increase vetting, reduce overstays, and determine whether nonimmigrants are complying with the conditions of their nonimmigrant classification. The requirements imposed by this final rule provides the U.S. government more opportunities to review a nonimmigrant's records, admissibility, and any possible indicators of fraud, abuse, or national security concerns. This rule seeks to address vulnerabilities posed by the D/S framework by providing DHS predetermined points in time for immigration officers to directly evaluate whether F, J, and I nonimmigrants are maintaining their status, as DHS does for other nonimmigrant classifications.
国土安全部认识到，学生完成本科和研究生课程的时间可能超过四年。国土安全部也注意到评论者提及的其他与高等教育完成相关的联邦标准，其规定的期限也超过四年，例如综合高等教育数据系统（Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System）和联邦助学金资格（Federal Financial Aid eligibility）标准。然而，本规则制定并不要求必须在四年内完成学业。相反，四年期限旨在作为一种执法和审查工具，用以评估学生是否保持正常的学业进度并符合F-1身份资格。能够证明持续取得学业进展并符合F-1资格标准的学生，可以申请延长身份（EOS）以完成其课程，这符合美国高等教育的实际情况。该学生也可以在完成剩余课程所需的准许停留期限内旅行并重新入境（印刷页45002）。此做法旨在加强审查与核实机制，而非设定僵化的完成期限。
DHS recognizes students may take longer than four years to complete their undergraduate and graduate programs of study. DHS also recognizes commenters' statements about other federal standards related to postsecondary education completion which are greater than four years, such as the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System and the Federal Financial Aid eligibility. However, this rulemaking does not require completion of a program within four years. Rather, the four-year period is intended as a law enforcement and screening tool to assess whether a student is maintaining normal academic progress and eligibility for F-1 status. Students who demonstrate continued academic progress and meet F-1 eligibility criteria may apply for an EOS to complete their programs, consistent with the realities of U.S. higher education. The student may also travel and reenter with a period of admission to complete the ( printed page 45002) remaining program of study. This approach is designed to enhance screening and vetting, not to impose a rigid completion deadline.
国土安全部(DHS)认识到对本规则可能对学术研究产生负面影响的担忧。然而，国土安全部认为，合法的外国籍研究人员将继续基于美国机构和项目的卓越性，寻求在美国的教育和研究机会。只要个别学生遵守其非移民身份的条款，本规则中的任何内容都不会妨碍学生继续其学习和研究。长期以来的政策（该政策并未改变）允许F-1和J-1学生在其身份延期（EOS）申请待决期间继续学习。本规则确实为校内就业、课程实习训练（CPT）以及因严重经济困难而从事的校外工作新增了一项规定，允许那些受雇者在其居留期限届满后，只要其已及时提交身份延期申请且该申请仍在美国公民及移民服务局（USCIS）待决，便可继续为同一雇主工作长达240天。本最终规则不改变8 CFR 274a.12(b)(6)(iv)中关于非移民学生从选择性实习训练（OPT）过渡到科学、技术、工程和数学（STEM）领域OPT的现行规定，前提是其已及时为其就业授权文件（EAD）申请延期，且该申请仍在USCIS待决。此类学生可在其OPT EAD到期后继续为同一雇主工作长达180天。该EAD延期可能与申请EOS的需求相吻合，也可能不吻合。如果相吻合，只要其已及时提交EOS申请，将被视为维持其身份，且该180天只有在其EAD到期后才开始计算。
DHS acknowledges the concern about potential negative impacts of the rule on academic research. However, DHS believes that legitimate foreign national researchers will continue to seek educational and research opportunities in the United States based on the excellence of United States institutions and programs. Nothing in this rule would prevent students from continuing their studies and research as long as individual students are complying with the terms of their nonimmigrant classification. Long-standing policy, which is not changing, allows F-1 and J-1 students to continue their studies for as long as their EOS application is pending. This rule does add a provision for on-campus employment, CPT, and off-campus work due to severe economic hardship which allows those who are employed to continue to work for the same employer up to 240 days after the expiration of their stay if they timely filed an EOS and it is still pending with USCIS. This final rule does not change the current regulations at 8 CFR 274a.12(b)(6)(iv) for nonimmigrant students transitioning from OPT to STEM OPT who have timely filed for an extension of their EAD, and it is pending with USCIS. They may continue to work for the same employer for up to 180 days after the expiration of their OPT EAD. This extension of the EAD may or may not coincide with a need to file for an EOS. If it does, they will be considered to be maintaining their status as long as they timely filed for the EOS and the 180 days will begin to toll only upon the expiration of their EAD.
国土安全部并未改变获得这些非移民身份资格的基本要求，仅改变个人在未提交身份延期（EOS）申请的情况下可合法在美国以F或J身份停留的期限。此外，正如固定准许停留期政策普遍适用的情况一样，固定的准许停留截止日期只是使这些非移民人员与大多数在美国临时停留的其他非移民人员处于相同的地位。他们仍将能够继续完成其完整的学业课程或交流项目。然而，如果他们需要在F或J身份下获得额外时间，现在责任将落在他们身上，需直接向国土安全部申请授权，并证明其有资格延长此类身份的停留期限，而此前他们是通过指定学校官员（DSO）或责任官员（RO）随项目延期一并获得合法身份延期的。因此，国土安全部认为本规则不会给学生或学校造成不当负担。
DHS is not changing the fundamental requirements to qualify for these nonimmigrant statuses; it is only changing the length of time that an individual may lawfully remain in the United States in F or J status without filing an EOS. Further, as is the case for the fixed period of admission policy more generally, a fixed date of admission simply places these nonimmigrants in the same position as most other nonimmigrants who are temporarily in the United States. They will still be able to continue to pursue their full course of study or exchange program. However, if they need additional time in F or J status, the burden will now be on them to request authorization directly from DHS and establish eligibility to extend their period of stay in such status, whereas previously they obtained an extension of lawful status in conjunction with a program extension through a DSO or RO. As such, DHS believes this rule will not cause undue burden to students or schools.
意见：许多评论者讨论了本规则对各行业造成的财务影响。在教育领域，评论者指出外国学生对美国做出的重大贡献，特别是在解决关键劳动力短缺问题方面，以及作为学生领袖、教学和科研助理、导师和辅导员所发挥的作用。与此相关，一位评论者援引国际教育交流的具体实例指出，这种学术交流每年为两国的教育机构及更广泛的经济体贡献数亿美元。
Comments: Many commenters discussed the rule's financial impact on various industries across the board. In the field of education, commenters remarked on the significant contributions of foreign students to the United States, particularly in addressing critical workforce shortages and as student leaders, teaching and research assistants, mentors, and tutors. Relatedly, a commenter, citing specific examples of international educational exchange, stated that this academic exchange contributes hundreds of millions of dollars annually to educational institutions and broader economies in both countries.
在STEM领域，评论者指出外国学生在STEM领域发挥的关键作用，指出他们在电气工程、计算机科学和数学等学科的研究生中占相当大的比例。评论者表示，美国大学协会（Association of American Universities）的数据显示，73%的国际STEM研究生毕业多年后仍继续在美国生活和工作，为美国提供科学、技术和经济效益。与此相关，评论者补充说，外国出生人士占美国博士级科学家和工程师的43%，而全国顶尖科学、工程和医学院的成员中，每三人中就有一人是归化美国公民。一位评论者指出，外国学生占统计学、计算机科学和健康信息学专业研究生入学人数的38%。评论者建议，招收主修STEM专业的外国学生应作为人才引进的主要渠道，因为美国面临严重的科技专业人才短缺问题，而这一短缺在短期内不太可能由美国本土学生填补。
In the STEM fields, commenters remarked on the critical role of foreign students in STEM fields, stating that they comprise a significant percentage of graduate students in disciplines such as electrical engineering, computer science, and mathematics. Commenters indicated that the data from the Association of American Universities showed that 73 percent of international STEM graduates continue to live and work in the United States years after graduation, providing scientific, technological, and economic benefits. Relatedly, commenters added that foreign-born individuals comprise 43 percent of doctorate-level scientists and engineers in the United States, and one in three members of the nation's leading science, engineering, and medical academies are naturalized U.S. citizens. A commenter stated that foreign students account for 38 percent of graduate enrollments in statistics, computer science and health informatics programs. Commenters suggested that recruiting foreign students majoring in STEM should serve as the primary channel for talent acquisition, as the United States faces a significant shortage of tech professionals unlikely to be filled by American students in the near term.
有评论者表示担忧,认为该拟议规则将对美国STEM(科学、技术、工程和数学)劳动力和领导地位产生负面影响,而据预测,2023年至2033年间STEM相关工作岗位将增长约10%,增速几乎是非STEM岗位的三倍,未来十年将产生87万个STEM职位需求。与此相关,评论者指出现有的劳动力短缺问题,包括半导体行业每年短缺2500名拥有高级工程学位的工作人员,以及预计未来十年制造工程师需求将增长14%,医疗数据分析师职位需求将增长31%,可再生能源相关职位将增长50%。评论者警告称,该拟议规则可能会促使顶尖学生和学者流向竞争国家,从而削弱美国在研究、医疗保健(包括老年护理)、人工智能(AI)和能源领域的领导地位。此外,评论者表示该政策可能削弱网络安全行业,从而使美国面临安全隐患。
Commenters expressed concern that the proposed rule would negatively impact the U.S. STEM workforce and leadership at a time when STEM jobs are projected to grow approximately 10 percent between 2023 and 2033—nearly three times faster than non-STEM jobs—creating a need for 870,000 STEM positions over the next decade. Relatedly, commenters pointed to existing labor shortages, including an annual deficit of 2,500 workers with advanced engineering degrees in the semiconductor industry, and a projected 14 percent increase in the need for manufacturing engineers, a 31 percent growth in the need for healthcare data analyst roles, and a 50 percent growth in renewable energy roles over the next decade. Commenters warned that the proposed rule could undermine U.S. leadership in research, healthcare, including elder care, artificial intelligence (AI), and energy by driving top students and scholars to competitor nations. Additionally, commentors stated that the policy may weaken the cybersecurity industry which would also leave the United States vulnerable.
有评论者表示,该拟议规则将威胁到其他关键行业,如金融服务、工程、云计算、生物技术、医疗保健分析、自动驾驶汽车、会计和量子计算。许多评论者就外国学生的作用、劳动力短缺及跨学科教育需求对以下行业提出了类似担忧:电信业、生物技术与医疗信息学、制药研发、金融科技(包括区块链、人工智能和数字支付)、医疗技术、保险与风险管理、法律服务与专业咨询、航空航天与国防系统、工业工程、汽车技术、计算机科学、环境修复与可持续发展、半导体、人才招聘,以及市场营销与供应链管理。一位评论者建议针对美国外国投资委员会所确定的供应链关键行业实施战略产业豁免,或者另行设立“国家经济安全”认定,允许在被认定为国内制造业关键领域工作的个人延长停留期限(D/S)。还有一位评论者论及外国学生在行为健康和社会工作领域所发挥的作用,指出国际心理学博士受训人员为服务不足社区提供有监督的护理,国际视角拓宽了社会工作研究的专业广度。另一位评论者补充说,社会工作专业毕业生常常通过OPT(选择性实习训练)或高级研究职位留下来为高需求社区服务,这有助于满足预计2024年至2034年间社会工作岗位6%的增长率,预计将创造超过74,000个新职位。
Commenters stated that the proposed rule would threaten other critical industries such as financial services, engineering, cloud computing, biotechnology, healthcare analytics, autonomous vehicles, accounting, and quantum computing. Many commentors stated similar concerns with the role of foreign students, worker deficit, and need for multidisciplinary education facing the industries for telecommunications; biotechnology and healthcare informatics; pharmaceutical development; fintech including blockchain, AI and digital payments; medical technology; insurance and risk management; legal services and professional consulting; aerospace and defense systems; industrial engineering; automotive technology; computer science; environmental remediation and sustainable development; semiconductors; talent acquisition; and marketing and supply chain management. A commenter suggested the implementation of strategic industries exemption for supply chain critical sectors identified by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States or alternatively create a “National Economic Security” designation allowing for extended D/S for individuals working in sectors deemed essential for domestic manufacturing. A commenter also addressed the role of foreign students in behavioral health and social work fields, stating that international doctoral psychology trainees provide supervised care to underserved communities, and international perspectives broaden expertise in social work research. Another commenter added that social work graduates often remain to serve high-need communities through OPT or advanced research positions, helping to meet the projected 6 percent growth in social work jobs from 2024-34, which is expected to create over 74,000 new positions.
另外,一位评论者特别表达了担忧,指出外国学生是纽约移民律师事务所、担保及中介机构(印刷页第45003页)以及房屋租赁平台的重要客户来源。同样,另一位评论者对该规则在纽约西部(包括布法罗地区)的影响表示担忧,并表示F-1学生贡献了2.491亿美元,并支持了2114个工作岗位。[135]
Separately, a commenter specifically expressed concern that foreign students represent a significant portion of clients for New York immigration law firms, sponsorship and intermediary agencies, ( printed page 45003) and housing rental platforms. Similarly, another commenter expressed concern on the impact of the rule in Western New York, including Buffalo, and stated that F-1 students contribute $249.1 million and support 2,114 jobs.[135]
回应:国土安全部(DHS)承认评论者所述外国学生和专业人士可为研究、技术发展和经济带来益处的观点。国土安全部也承认外国学生在STEM和技术专业学生中占比很高。然而,国土安全部认为,部分评论者将入境许可期限与外国学生为完成学业而被允许在美国停留的总时间相混淆。如果学生需要超出其最初入境许可期限的额外时间以完成学业,则可以通过向美国公民及移民服务局(USCIS)提交延长身份申请(EOS)来延长其身份,或者,如果其选择出境旅行,可凭有效签证通过美国海关与边境保护局(CBP)在入境口岸(POE)申请入境,并获得附有新授权停留期限(AUD)的新I-94表。鉴于存在延长身份的多种途径,国土安全部认为无需基于特定行业设立豁免。国土安全部预计外国学生将继续在STEM领域追求教育机会。
Response: DHS acknowledges commenters' assertions that foreign students and professionals can provide benefits to research, technology developments, and the economy. DHS also acknowledges that foreign students make up a high percentage of students in STEM and technology programs. However, DHS believes some commenters are conflating the admission period with the total amount of time a foreign student may be permitted to remain in the United States to complete a program. Students who require additional time beyond their initial period of admission to complete their program may be eligible to extend their status by filing an EOS application with USCIS or, if they choose to travel, they can (with an unexpired visa) apply for admission at a POE through CBP and receive a new I-94 with a new AUD. Given the options for extending status, DHS does not believe it is necessary to create exemptions based on certain industries. DHS expects that foreign students will continue to pursue educational opportunities in the STEM fields.
c. 财务影响与行政负担
c. Financial Impact and Administrative Burden
评论:评论者对该规则给高等教育机构、大学运营带来的财务影响和行政负担、削弱协作性学术环境、以及可能迫使学校违背在学生招募过程中做出的承诺表示担忧。多名评论者指出,大学依赖可预测的签证政策进行财务、人员配备和资源规划,而拟议规则中要求固定入学期限的突然、僵化变化,会造成不可持续的行政负担和法律风险,并使SEVIS(学生和交流访问者信息系统)下的合规报告复杂化,可能威胁整个行业的稳定性。
Comments: Commenters expressed concern regarding the rule's financial impact and administrative burden on higher education institutions, university operations, diminished collaborative academic environments, and the potential to force schools to break promises made during student recruitment. Multiple commenters pointed out that universities rely on predictable visa policies for financial, staffing, and resource planning and that sudden, rigid changes in the proposed rule requiring fixed admission periods create unsustainable administrative burdens, legal risks, and complicate compliance reporting under SEVIS that could threaten the stability of the entire sector.
关于成本问题,评论者表示,国土安全部(DHS)分析估计的67小时低估了真实影响,因为拟议规则将从根本上改变指定学校官员(DSO)和责任官员(RO)工作的范围,要求他们彻底改革日常流程,向学生宣讲新要求,并与校园利益相关方进行协调。少数评论者指出,DSO将不得不接受额外培训和适应,以熟悉新法规,预计这项合规成本在第一年将达到全行业9330万美元。[136] 与此相关,一位自称是公立大学教育管理人员的评论者估计,培训、软件更新和新增人员配置需要超过1000小时和25万美元。另一位评论者表示,由于拟议规则,机构需要为“资源的大规模扩充”做好准备,包括为应对新系统的学生加强法律和心理健康支持。一位评论者特别指出,根据他们的初步分析,该规则将要求俄克拉荷马州立大学额外聘用四名全职移民合规人员,并实施新的跟踪系统,初始成本约为50万美元。
With respect to costs, commenters stated that the 67-hour estimate by DHS analysis underestimated the true impact, as the proposed rule would fundamentally alter the scope of DSO and RO work, requiring them to overhaul routine processes, educate students on new requirements, and coordinate with campus stakeholders. A few commenters pointed out that DSOs would have to undergo additional training and adaptation to familiarize themselves with the new regulations, and that this compliance cost is estimated to reach $93.3 million across the sector in year one.[136] Relatedly, a commenter who identified as an education administrator at a public university estimated needing over 1,000 hours and $250,000 for training, software updates, and new staffing. Another commenter remarked that institutions would need to prepare for a “massive scaling of resources,” including enhanced legal and mental health support for students navigating the new system, because of the proposed rule. A commenter specifically remarked that the rule would require Oklahoma State University to hire four additional full-time immigration compliance staff and implement new tracking systems costing approximately $500,000 initially, based on their preliminary analysis.
多名评论者表示,拟议规则将使DSO工作超负荷,延误处理,并增加意外失去身份的违规情况,并指出美国教育理事会已对拟议规则提出警告(未提供出处)。多名评论者指出,教育机构工作量的增加将导致员工职业倦怠和DSO人员更高的离职率,由于员工经验不足,机构不合规的风险会增加。另一位评论者指出,由于学生根据学年日历和I-20表格到期日在相近时间提交申请,该规则的行政负担将因此加剧。与此相关,一位评论者表示,拟议规则假定DSO和责任官员助理(ARO)将为学生和交流访问者提供I-539表格申请协助,但许多学校不允许其官员从事此类工作,因为这可能构成未经授权的法律执业。该评论者对学校是否应聘请法律助理代表学生提交延期居留(EOS)表格,还是学生和交流访问者需要自行承担此类费用表示不确定,并对此表示担忧。
Multiple commenters stated that the proposed rule will overload DSOs, delay processing, and increase accidental out-of-status violations, and noted that the American Council on Education has warned against the proposed rule (no source provided). Several commenters noted that the increased workload on the educational institutions would lead to staff burnout and higher turnover rates with DSO staff, increasing the risk of institutional non-compliance due to less experienced staff. Another commenter noted that the rule's administrative burden would be exacerbated by students filing at similar times based on academic calendars and I-20 end dates. Relatedly, a commenter stated that the proposed rule assumes that DSOs and AROs will provide students and exchange visitors with Form I-539 application support, but that many schools do not allow their officials to undertake this work, as it could constitute unauthorized practice of law. The commenter voiced concern about the uncertainty on whether the school should be hiring legal assistants to file EOS forms on behalf of students or if the students and exchange visitors would need to assume such costs.
一位评论者指出,国土安全部估计每位DSO需要67小时培训,每位DSO成本为3342美元,另加每份延期居留(EOS)申请233美元。同一位评论者表示,即使入学人数小幅下降也可能造成重大损失,因为根据国际教育协会(IIE)的数据(未提供出处),外国学生在2022至2023年为美国经济贡献了401亿美元,支持了368,333个美国就业岗位。
A commenter noted that DHS estimates 67 hours of training per DSO, which costs $3,342 per DSO, plus $233 per EOS request. The same commenter stated that even modest enrollment declines could cause major losses because foreign students contributed $40.1 billion to the U.S. economy in 2022-23, supporting 368,333 U.S. jobs, according to the Institute of International Education (IIE) (no source provided).
回应:国土安全部承认,管理人员和参与者都需要一定的学习适应期来熟悉新规则。这正是设立60天实施期和4年过渡期的原因。在规则生效时处于“在读期限”(D/S)身份的人员,将有长达4年的时间在美国境内完成其项目,而无需转换为确定日期的身份。只有在规则生效日期之后抵达的参与者才须遵守规则的所有规定。管理人员将在60天实施期内获得充分培训,以了解如何应对和帮助受新规则约束的新入境参与者。SEVIS系统将进行更新,以便于规则的实施。因此,国土安全部认为评论者的担忧不会成为现实。
Response: DHS acknowledges that there will be learning curve for both administrators and participants to get accustomed to the new rule. That is why there is a 60-day implementation period and a 4-year transition period. Those in D/S status when the rule takes effect will have up to 4 years to finish their programs without changing to a date certain while living in the United States. Only participants arriving after the effective date of the rule will be subject to all the provisions of the rule. Administrators will receive plenty of training during the 60-day implementation period to understand how to deal with and help incoming participants subject to the new rule. SEVIS will be updated to make the implementation of the rule easier. Therefore, DHS does not believe that the commenters fears will come to fruition.
针对提供学校/交流项目指定官员(DSO/RO)劳动负担替代估算的意见,国土安全部(DHS)已将规则熟悉与适应负担估算从67小时修订为公众意见提供的中位数值135小时。此增加已反映在更新后的成本数字中,并包括因本规则而产生的任何额外培训或材料制作。国土安全部预计,大多数获授权担保F类学生和J类交流访问学者的学校将能够以现有员工应对额外的DSO/RO劳动负担,因为提交延长居留期(EOS)申请的大部分负担将落在受本规则约束的非移民身上。学校承担的负担仍已作为量化成本纳入监管影响分析之中。然而,国土安全部认识到,部分学校可能选择聘用更多DSO和RO以满足本规则制定的要求。国土安全部预计,雇用成本将因各机构的F类学生和J类交流访问学者人数、机构规模及现有员工人数而异。尽管如此,国土安全部预计,对于绝大多数机构担保方而言,雇用及支付额外员工薪酬的成本仅占其年收入的一小部分。请参阅本规则制定案卷中提供的监管影响分析(RIA)。
In response to comments providing alternative estimates for the DSO/RO labor burden, DHS has revised the rule familiarization and adaptation burden estimate from 67 hours to the median value the public comments provided of 135 hours. This increase is reflected in the updated cost numbers, and includes any additional training or materials created due to this rule. DHS anticipates that most schools authorized to sponsor F students and J exchange visitors will be able to accommodate the additional DSO/RO labor burden with existing staff, as much of the burden for filing EOS requests will fall to the nonimmigrants subject to this rule. The burden to the school has still been accounted for in the regulatory impact analysis as a quantified cost. DHS, however, recognizes that some schools may elect to hire more DSOs and ROs to meet the requirements of this rulemaking. DHS expects hiring costs to vary depending on the number of F students and J exchange visitors at each institution, the size of the institution, and the number of existing staff. That said, DHS anticipates that costs of hiring and paying additional staff will represent a small portion of annual revenue for the great majority of institutional sponsors. See Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA), available in the docket for this rulemaking.
此外,与本规则相关的其他成本,例如用于批量处理的系统升级费用,已被确认,但在监管影响分析中(印刷版第45004页)仍未量化。这些成本因负责F类和J类签证事务的各实体而异,因为目前尚不清楚有多少团体使用会产生较高费用的专有软件,相对于可能仅需低成本升级即可继续使用的现成软件。因此,由于差异性较大且缺乏可提供有意义估算的具体数据,国土安全部选择不对这些软件成本进行量化。这些成本仍以定性方式加以讨论。
Additionally, other costs associated with this rule, such as system upgrades for batch processing, are acknowledged but remain unquantified in the ( printed page 45004) Regulatory Impact Analysis. These costs will be variable to each entity responsible for F and J visas, as it is unclear how many groups use proprietary software that would incur larger expenses versus off-the-shelf software that may come with a low-cost upgrade to continue functionality. Therefore, due to the high variance and lack of specific data to provide a meaningful estimate, DHS has chosen to not quantify these software costs. These costs are still discussed in a qualitative fashion.
针对有关机构需要为“资源的大规模扩充”做准备的担忧意见,包括为应对新系统的学生提供加强的法律和心理健康支持,国土安全部认为无需进行此类大规模扩充。国土安全部承认,部分机构可能选择提供额外服务,例如法律和心理健康支持,但这些额外服务并非本规则的要求。国土安全部将提供资源和培训,以协助相关利益相关方遵守本规则。由于学生和交流访问学者获得的支持和资源因学校和项目担保方而异,国土安全部无法对其影响进行定性估算。
In response to comments expressing concern about the need for institutions to prepare for a “massive scaling of resources,” including enhanced legal and mental health support for students navigating the new system, DHS does not believe such massive scaling will be necessary. DHS recognizes some institutions may choose to provide additional services, such as legal and mental health support, but these additional services are not a requirement of this rule. DHS will provide resources and training to assist relevant stakeholders in complying with the rule. Because support and resources for students and exchange visitors vary widely by school and program sponsor, DHS cannot qualitatively estimate the impact.
国土安全部不同意本规则将导致意外失去身份违规行为的说法。将提供资源和指导,以协助DSO、RO、学生及交流访问学者熟悉并遵守本规则的要求。规则生效后意外违反身份的学生或交流访问学者,仍可申请恢复其非移民身份。非移民是否认为需要法律专业人士协助填写表格,将由个人自行决定。表格采用符合《简明语言法》指引的清晰语言撰写,并配有旨在易于理解的说明。
DHS disagrees with the assertion that the rule will lead to accidental out-of-status violations. Resources and guidance will be available to assist DSOs, ROs, students, and exchange visitors in familiarizing themselves and complying with the rule's requirements. Students or exchange visitors who accidentally violate their status after the rule takes effect will still have the ability to apply for reinstatement of their nonimmigrant status. Whether or not nonimmigrants feel they will need the help of a legal professional to fill out the forms will be a personal decision. The forms are written in clear language adhering to the guidelines of the Plain Language Act with instructions designed to be easy to understand.
意见:部分评论者对因非移民学生及学者入学人数下降而对机构造成的财务影响表示担忧。许多评论者写道,外国学生按全额学费缴费有助于通过补贴方式维持本国学生可负担的大学入学机会。
Comments: Commenters voiced concerns regarding the financial impact on institutions resulting from the drop in nonimmigrant student and scholar enrollment. Many commenters wrote that foreign students' full-price tuition helps maintain affordable college access for domestic students by subsidizing them.
具体而言,一家律师协会指出,2015年私立大学从国际硕士生身上获得了43亿美元的收入,公立大学获得了30亿美元,这在很大程度上可归因于以下事实:外国学生缴纳全额学费或外州学费,通常是州内学费的两到三倍。[137]一位评论者表示,大型公立大学依赖外国学生缴纳的较高学费来弥补州政府拨款的减少。同样,其他评论者对以下情况表示担忧:外国学生流失带来的财务风险将不成比例地影响依赖外国学生及其学费收入的私立、规模较小、信仰型或地区性院校。一位来自信仰型院校的评论者详细说明,外国学生对其“以基督为本”的使命至关重要,而且外国学生往往来自宗教受限地区。另一位评论者表示,非精英大学没有本国学生候补名单来弥补这一流失的学费收入。
Specifically, a lawyers association noted that private universities received $4.3 billion in revenue from international master's students in 2015, and public universities received $3 billion, much of which can be attributed to the fact that foreign students pay full or out-of-state tuition, which is usually two to three times more than in-state tuition.[137] A commenter stated that large public universities depend on the higher tuition paid by foreign students to offset declining state funding. Similarly, other commenters expressed concern that the financial risk of foreign student losses would disproportionately affect private, smaller, faith-based, or regional colleges that rely on a high proportion of foreign students and their tuition revenue. A commenter from a faith-based institution elaborated that foreign students are vital to their “Christ based” mission and that often, foreign students come from religiously restricted regions. Another commenter stated that non-elite universities do not have waiting lists of domestic students to make up for this lost tuition revenue.
一位评论者援引穆迪公司[138]的一项估计,该估计发现,国际入学率下降20%将对130所院校的运营利润率产生负面影响,使其下降半个百分点,其中18所院校的利润率将损失2%至8%。该评论者解释说,这种损失可能会给利润率已经微薄的院校带来重大财务压力。此外,多位评论者补充说,学费收入的损失将导致机构为所有学生提供的课程和服务被削减,通过提高学费或减少经济援助来将成本转嫁给本国学生,或影响学校运营的其他方面,可能危及其持续运营。一些评论者还对用于资助前沿研究计划以及教职员工岗位的学费收入损失表示担忧。
One commenter cited an estimate from Moody's [138] which found that a 20 percent drop in international enrollment would negatively affect operating margins at 130 institutions by half a percentage point, with 18 institutions losing between 2 to 8 percent. This commenter explained that such loss could trigger significant financial stress for colleges with already thin margins. Additionally, several commenters added that lost tuition income would result in cuts to institutional offerings and services for all students, passing costs on to domestic students by raising tuition rates or reducing financial aid offers, or impacting other aspects of a school's operations, potentially compromising its continuity. Some commenters also expressed concern about the loss of tuition revenue for funding cutting-edge research initiatives and faculty or staff positions.
在解释财务损失时,一位评论者引用了一项分析[139],该分析说明,全国平均每位居民所承受的负面经济影响为130美元,但华盛顿特区以及马萨诸塞州、纽约州、罗德岛州和康涅狄格州等州的影响会更高,其中华盛顿特区估计为每位居民855美元。
In explaining the financial loss, one commenter pointed to an analysis [139] that explained that the national negative economic impact would be on average $130 per resident, but Washington, DC and states such as Massachusetts, New York, Rhode Island, and Connecticut would be even higher, with Washington, DC estimated at $855 per resident.
回应:美国国土安全部(DHS)承认评论者关于外国学生和专业人士能够带来经济利益的主张。DHS认为,这种经济贡献在最终规则生效后将继续累积,因为外国学生将继续选择在美国留学。尽管DHS承认该规则可能会减少非移民学生的入学人数,特别是在那些试图违反法定和法规意图的外国国民中,但DHS认为,非移民学生仍将来到美国,因为美国仍然是科学研究、创新和技术领域的世界领导者,为学生提供接触前沿设施和项目的机会。DHS不认为本最终规则会对信仰型院校或来自宗教受限地区的学生产生影响。尽管该规则对转学和项目变更设置了一些限制,但该规则根据学生和交流访问者项目(SEVP)授权,为特殊情况设置了例外。参见新8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(ii)(A)。
Response: DHS acknowledges commenters' assertions that foreign students and professionals can provide economic benefits. DHS asserts that such economic contributions will continue to accrue after the final rule becomes effective because foreign students will continue to choose to study in the United States. While DHS acknowledges that the rule may decrease nonimmigrant student enrollments, particularly among foreign nationals seeking to violate statutory and regulatory intent, DHS believes that, nonimmigrant students will still come to the United States because the United States remains the world leader in scientific research, innovation, and technology, providing students with access to cutting-edge facilities and projects. DHS does not believe that this final rule will have an impact on faith-based institutions nor students coming from religiously restricted regions. While the rule creates some restrictions on transfers and program changes, the rule creates exceptions for extenuating circumstances based on SEVP authorization. See new 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(ii)(A).
由于多种因素在学生决定何时何地入学方面发挥作用,本规则在多大程度上可能阻碍非移民学生来美是带有推测性且难以预测的。[140]有关入学影响不确定性的详细讨论,参见监管影响分析(RIA)附录A。美国在研发方面投入巨大,拥有世界知名的大学和研究机构,并且是众多领先科技公司的所在地。美国在医学、工程学、太空探索、信息技术和人工智能等领域持续取得重大进展,这些领域对所有学生都具有吸引力。[141]
It is speculative and difficult to predict the extent to which nonimmigrant students may be deterred from coming to the United States based on this rule when a variety of factors play a role in a student determining when and where to enroll.[140] See a detailed discussion on uncertainty related to enrollment impacts in Appendix A of the RIA. The United States invests heavily in research and development, has world-renowned universities and research institutions, and is home to many leading technology companies. The United States consistently produces significant advancements in fields such as medicine, engineering, space exploration, information technology, and artificial intelligence that are attractive for all students.[141]
最后,针对有评论者认为国际学生在美国院校入学率下降将导致本国学生学费上涨的意见,基于上述原因,国土安全部(DHS)认为,预测本终局规则将如何影响非移民学生的入学人数及美国院校(第45005页)的财务运作具有推测性且难以预测。[142]美国院校如何评定学费并从本国及外国学生中获取收入,以及如何利用捐赠基金或捐款等其他收入来源,是每个院校自主作出的商业决策。[143]捐赠基金规模可能相当可观,每年可达数百万、数十亿甚至数百亿美元。[144]这些资金来源独立于非移民学生所带来的收入。
Finally, in response to commenters who said that declining international enrollment in U.S. institutions will increase tuition costs for domestic students, for the reasons stated above, DHS maintains that it is speculative and difficult to predict how this final rule will affect enrollment numbers for nonimmigrant students and the financial operations of U.S. ( printed page 45005) institutions.[142] How a U.S. institution assesses tuition and obtains income from students both domestic and foreign, along with other sources of income such as endowments or donations, is a business decision that each institution has the autonomy to make.[143] Endowments can be substantial and may amount to millions, billions, or even tens of billions of dollars per year.[144] These funding sources are independent of the revenue derived from nonimmigrant students.
国土安全部无法准确预测院校为应对非移民入学人数可能下降并影响其财务状况而可能采取的行动。美国院校每年都自主作出有关入学事宜的商业决策,例如班级规模和组成。[145]这些商业决策可能影响在特定美国院校就读的外国学生人数,并且这些商业决策可能是针对外国学生和美国学生入学人数的减少或增加而作出的。
DHS is unable to accurately forecast which actions institutions may take to address the possibility that nonimmigrant enrollment may decline and impact their financial health. U.S. institutions autonomously make business decisions every year about enrollment such as the class size and composition.[145] These business decisions can impact the number of foreign students enrolled at a particular U.S. institution and those business decisions may be made in response to decreasing or increasing enrollment of both foreign and U.S. students.
d. 教育质量与跨文化效益
d. Quality of Education and Cross-Cultural Benefits
评论意见:评论者指出,拟议规则将使企业更难招募到特别熟悉亚洲、拉丁美洲和欧洲等增长市场的人才。一位评论者提到杜克大学的一项研究[146],该研究发现,美国学生在与外国学生经常互动时,“据报告具有更强的自信心、领导能力、量化能力和跨文化理解力”。许多评论者表示,外国学生的存在促进了相互尊重、合作、文化善意和软实力外交。另一位评论者表示,双语交流项目通过使学生为多语言环境做好准备而有益于经济发展。
Comments: Commenters stated that the proposed rule would make it harder for companies to recruit talent who are especially familiar with growth markets in places such as Asia, Latin America, and Europe. One commenter noted a Duke University study [146] which found that U.S. students “reported greater self-confidence, leadership skills, quantitative abilities, and cross-cultural understanding” when they interacted with foreign students on a regular basis. Many commenters stated that foreign student presence fosters mutual respect, collaboration, cultural goodwill, and soft diplomacy. Another commenter stated that dual language exchange programs benefit the economy by preparing students for multilingual environments.
评论者强调,外国学生支持并增加了本国学生的课程选择,维持了本国学生兴趣不足学科的入学人数,特别是在STEM(科学、技术、工程和数学)领域,从而为所有学生创造并维持了学术机会,包括关键学科的机会。
Commenters emphasized that foreign students support and increase class options for domestic students, sustaining enrollments in disciplines with insufficient domestic interest, particularly STEM fields, and thereby creating and maintaining academic opportunities for all students, including opportunities in critical disciplines.
许多评论者表示,外国学生充当非正式大使,形成了有机的文化交流,使美国学生和外国学生都受益,并加强了国际关系。多位评论者表示,外国学生往往成为其本国的政治或商业领袖,二十国集团(G20)国家中现任外交部长、贸易官员或高级外交官中,有34%曾持F或J签证在美国留学。截至2022年,已有41位世界领导人曾在美国接受教育。一位评论者解释说,当外国学生成为未来的全球领袖时,他们在美国求学期间建立的关系可能有助于其对美国利益的投入和认同。另一位评论者指出,外国学生的存在推进了1961年《富布赖特-海斯法案》所设想的目标,通过促进相互理解和在全球建立人与人之间的联系来加强外交关系。一位评论者表示,拟议规则将破坏美国国务院(DoS)BridgeUSA项目[147]的使命和理念,该项目的宗旨是“通过教育和文化交流增进美国人民与其他国家人民之间的相互理解”,而这将导致选择赴美留学并为美国经济作出贡献的人数减少,因此该项目应被豁免于本规则之外。
Many commenters stated that foreign students serve as unofficial ambassadors, creating an organic cultural exchange that benefits both American and foreign students and strengthening international relationships. Multiple commenters stated that foreign students often become political or business leaders in their home countries, with 34 percent of current foreign ministers, trade officials, or senior diplomats in G20 countries having studied in the United States on F or J visas. As of 2022, 41 world leaders had been educated in the United States. A commenter explained that when foreign students become future global leaders, the relationships they developed during their education in the United States could contribute to their investment in and alignment with American interests. Another commenter noted that the presence of foreign students advances the goals envisioned by the Fulbright-Hays Act of 1961, strengthening diplomacy by fostering mutual understanding and building people-to-people connections around the world. A commenter stated that the proposed rule would undermine the mission and philosophy of the DoS's BridgeUSA Program,[147] the purpose of which is “to increase mutual understanding between the people of the United States and the people of other countries by means of educational and cultural exchanges,” which in turn would lead to fewer individuals choosing to study in the United States and contribute to the U.S. economy, therefore, it should be exempt from this rule.
答复:国土安全部(DHS)承认与外国学生和交流访问者建立关系所带来的益处。国土安全部并不意图通过此项规则制定使国际招生出现显著下降,因此,国土安全部预计本规则不会损害美国在全球的伙伴关系,也不会显著影响美国公司招募熟悉全球增长市场人才的能力,或改变课程选择,尤其是在科学、技术、工程和数学(STEM)领域。国土安全部认为,美国教育机构将继续吸引科学、技术、工程和数学(STEM)及其他高需求领域的优秀外国学生、研究人员和学者,因为这些机构提供高质量的教育。美国院校在重视美国学位的外国学生中仍保持良好声誉,除获准以“在读期限”(D/S)身份入境外,还有许多其他因素使美国对非移民学生和交流访问者具有吸引力。国土安全部仍致力于支持《富布赖特-海斯法案》所设想的更广泛的教育与文化交流目标。
Response: DHS acknowledges the benefits of fostering relationships with foreign students and exchange visitors. DHS does not intend for this rulemaking to result in significant declines to international enrollment and, thus, DHS does not expect this rule to harm U.S. partnerships across the globe; significantly affect the ability of U.S. companies to recruit talent familiar with global growth markets; or change class options, particularly in STEM. DHS asserts that U.S. educational institutions will continue to attract talented foreign students, researchers, and scholars in STEM and other high-demand fields because such institutions offer a high-quality education. U.S. institutions remain reputable to foreign students who value a degree from a U.S. institution and there are many factors that have made the United States attractive to nonimmigrant students and exchange visitors beyond being admitted for D/S. DHS remains committed to supporting broader goals of educational and cultural exchange envisioned by the Fulbright-Hays Act.
6. 对美国经济、公民、产业、劳动力或社区的负面影响
6. Negative Impacts on the U.S. Economy, Citizens, Industries, Workforce, or Communities
a. 美国竞争力与国家政策目标
a. U.S. Competitiveness and National Policy Goals
评论意见:有评论者表示担忧,认为对外国学生和交流访问者的限制将损害美国在科学和技术领域的卓越地位和竞争力,可能使国际研究中心和就业机会转移至海外。一位评论者表示,人才和发展势头的流失将削弱美国的研究领先地位和临床基础设施,这可能损害国家安全和经济安全,同时也会导致美国培养的国际专业人才流失给全球竞争对手。[148] 其他评论者表示,这些限制将与《芯片与科学法案》所确立的国家政策目标相矛盾。[149] 一位评论者写道,不确定性和严格审查可能会使外国学生不愿从事高风险、高回报的长期基础研究或敏感但关键的领域研究,(printed page 45006)转而选择“更安全”的短期学习项目。此外,另一位评论者指出,从事此类领域研究的外国学生有助于支持美国的国防工业、研究实验室和科技行业,如果这些有技能的学生离开,美国在科技方面的竞争优势可能会被削弱。另一位评论者写道,他们认识到移民问题存在更广泛的关切,并指出虽然通过婚姻或庇护获得身份可能不一定符合美国的经济或技术目标,但F-1学生确实为美国的未来增添了价值。
